The statute treats the schedule as the whole fee and collects it before the document is filed. Call the office before you go to learn which payment types it takes.

Who covers the stamp tax on a Caldwell County sale?

The seller covers it. Per the county's FAQ, the grantor pays this stamp tax as the deed is lodged, and G.S. 105-228.30 assigns the duty to the transferor, to be paid to the register before filing.

  • It attaches to any instrument that conveys an interest in land.
  • The county and the state share what is collected.
  • The closing agent usually deducts the stamp amount from the seller's proceeds.
  • For a gift deed with no price, ask the office how it handles the stamp.

A cash sale follows the same rule. The sale price sets the amount, so agree on it with the closing attorney first.

What must a deed carry before the Caldwell County office files it?

The real estate page sets three conditions. Every deed must show the grantee's current mailing address. Any deed or deed of trust drawn in North Carolina must name its drafter on page one. If you want the original mailed back, enclose a prepaid, pre-addressed envelope.

The office scans each document when it is presented and hands it back or puts it in the outgoing mail, so there is no waiting period for a return. The state adopted recording standards in 2002 for page layout, and the office links to them from the same page. Look at them before printing, since a paper that misses the layout rules can be recorded only with the extra nonstandard fee.

The staff cannot fill in your forms or search title. Its FAQ confirms that you can write your own deed but recommends an attorney, and says a name can only be added to or removed from a deed by recording a new deed.

How do I search Caldwell County land records before I sell?

You can search them online from the register of deeds site. The county says every real estate index since the formation of the county is online, and images of the documents are online from the early 1900s forward.

Search for the vesting deed, any loan still open, and any easement or road maintenance agreement on the parcel. The office page names road maintenance agreements as a record type it holds, so check for one if your driveway is shared. If your copy is gone, the office can issue a sealed certified one.

  • Spot any loan never released, then request a payoff letter.
  • Confirm that every named co-owner will sign.
  • Look for recorded agreements that run with the land.

Everything on file is public except certified vital records and recent military discharges. A veteran can record a DD214 at no charge, which is how the county's Thank-a-Veteran discount card program starts.

How does the Caldwell County tax bill affect a closing?

Any unpaid county tax sits on the parcel as a lien, so it gets settled when the house closes. The Tax Office shares the Lenoir address, keeps the same weekday hours, and lists 828-757-1340 as its phone.

The tax staff of 19 work in six departments, and besides county tax they bill the rescue readiness charge, 14 fire districts and three municipalities: Sawmills, Rhodhiss and the Village of Cedar Rock. July is when bills arrive, with a 2% early-pay discount that month and 1% in August. September 1 is the due date, and January 5 closes the interest-free window.

The interest schedule in G.S. 105-360 starts at 2% on January 6 and then adds three-fourths of a percent monthly. Caldwell County went through a general reappraisal for 2025; its commissioners were told in February 2025 that the county's sales ratio had fallen below the 0.85 threshold in state law, and the appraisal was done by county staff for residential property. Ask the Tax Office for your parcel's current value and any rate adopted since.

Its site also carries a foreclosure list and an online listing portal for business and personal property, and card payments by phone go to 1-844-866-6645. Mail for the office goes to PO Box 2200, Lenoir, NC 28645.

How large is the Caldwell County housing market?

The July 2025 estimate is 81,105 residents, a 0.5% rise from the 2020 base, in 38,057 housing units. The land covers 471.89 square miles, or 170.9 people per square mile in 2020.

  • Middle-of-the-range owned home value: $192,200 (2020-2024), with owners living in 73.5% of units.
  • Median gross rent is $744, and the county counts 32,919 households averaging 2.42 people.
  • Building permits issued in 2025 numbered 501, and 4,370 residents are veterans.
  • Median household income is $56,425.

These numbers are published on the Census QuickFacts page for Caldwell County. Older residents make up 22.8% of the county. A senior or disabled owner on a modest income can ask the Tax Office about the state exclusion; the 2026 income ceiling is $38,800.

More questions about Caldwell County, NC Register of Deeds

Do I need a lawyer to file a deed with the Caldwell County register?

Yes, the FAQ allows it, though it urges hiring an attorney since staff cannot advise or search title. The deed must still show the grantee's mailing address and the drafter's name.

What are the hours of the Caldwell County Register of Deeds?

It opens at eight and closes at five on weekdays, at 905 West Avenue NW in Lenoir. New marriage license applications stop half an hour earlier.

Is the stamp tax on a Caldwell County sale my cost as the seller?

Yes. The county says the grantor pays $1.00 for each $500.00 of the price, and the statute names the transferor.

Does the Caldwell County register of deeds keep wills?

No, wills go to the Clerk of Court according to the county's FAQ. For an inherited house, take estate questions to the clerk and deed history questions here.

How far back do Caldwell County land records go?

Back to 1841, when the county was formed. Every real estate index is searchable online, and scanned images begin in the early 1900s.

Where does a Carteret County deed get filed?

The Register of Deeds takes deeds in the County Administrative Building, which stands at 302 Courthouse Square in Beaufort. Anyone can inspect records there on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.

The office calls itself the legal custodian of every land record and land transaction in the county, and it indexes and images each one into the permanent file. The county says the whole file is open to the public except military discharges. An online database lets you view and print land records from home, which is the fastest route to your vesting deed before listing.

One detail applies to older paperwork. The county's real estate page says Books 301 through 514 are on aperture cards, and a cancelled deed of trust is stamped on the card itself. If you need proof that an old loan was released and the online image does not show it, call the office rather than assuming the lien is still open.

What are the recording fees in Carteret County?

The county publishes one fee list, and its real estate lines track the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10. The office accepts cash, credit or debit card, money orders and cashier's checks for recording.

Document or serviceFee as the county prints it
General instruments other than deeds of trust and mortgages$26 covers 15 pages, then $4 a page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64 covers 35 pages, then $4 a page
Plats$21 per sheet
Satisfaction instrumentsNo fee per statute
Document containing multiple instrumentsAdditional $10
Nonstandard documentsAdditional $25
Certified copies$5 for page one, $2 per page after
Uncertified copies$0.25
Excise tax valuation$2 per $1000.00 of sales price

On the same list, each added index reference on an assignment adds $10 and a military discharge is recorded free. The page carries an October 1, 2019 effective date, so ask the office whether any line has changed since then.

How do I keep a Carteret County deed from being charged as nonstandard?

Follow the county's published recording standards, because a document that misses them is still recorded but costs an extra $25. The office's penalty paragraph says it will record the nonconforming document after collecting the $25 nonstandard fee along with the normal recording fee.

  • Page size: letter or legal.
  • First page: leave 3 inches blank across the top.
  • Remaining sides of page one and all sides of later pages: a 1/4 inch blank margin, per the standards page.
  • Print: black on white, in a legible font, with 10 points as the smallest size treated as legible.
  • Pages: one-sided only.
  • Title: name the kind of instrument at the head of page one.

The fee page contradicts the standards page on side margins. It says the minimum side margin went back to one-half inch under Session Law 2019-117, effective October 1, 2019, while the standards page still shows 1/4 inch. Ask the office which one it applies before you print the deed. Pen is acceptable for blanks and corrections, and the office may treat slightly small type as legible and skip the fee.

Who owes the stamp tax when a Carteret County house sells?

The seller owes it. As G.S. 105-228.30 reads, the transferor pays the register of deeds before the deed goes on record.

In the statute the rate is $1.00 for each $500.00, and a leftover fraction counts as a full unit. Carteret County's fee page expresses the same thing as $2 per $1000.00 of the sales price. On a settlement statement it shows on the seller's side, since the closing agent usually withholds it from the proceeds.

Filing matters as much as the tax. Per G.S. 47-18, a transfer is ineffective against lien creditors and paying purchasers until it is registered in the county of the land. A buyer who does not record leaves the door open to later claims.

What should I pull from the Carteret County records before listing?

Pull four items from the online database or the Beaufort counter: your vesting deed, every deed of trust that touches the parcel and its release if one exists, any plat for the lot, and recorded easements. Plats are priced by the sheet, at $21 each on the county's fee list, and map copies are $1.00 or $2.00 depending on size.

  • The vesting deed shows exactly how title is held, including any co-owners who must sign.
  • A recorded satisfaction shows that an old loan was released, and the county charges nothing to file one.
  • A plat or map tells you the lot lines before a buyer's survey does.
  • Uncertified copies cost $0.25 a page, so printing the record for your own file is cheap.

A recorded release is the proof a title company looks for. If the loan is paid and no release shows, ask the lender to file one rather than waiting for the buyer's title search to find the gap.

How do Carteret County property taxes figure into a sale?

Whatever tax is still open on the parcel gets paid out of the closing, so phone the Tax Administration Office on 252-728-8485 for the amount well ahead of the settlement table. That office sits in the same Beaufort building as the register of deeds, which makes it easy to handle both errands in one trip.

The register and the tax office do different jobs. The register records the deed and collects the stamp tax. The tax office bills the annual tax, hears value questions and tracks relief claims. Our Carteret County property tax guide covers due dates, interest, appeals and collection steps in detail.

What other papers does the Carteret County office handle for an inherited house?

Birth, death and marriage records for events in the county are also kept here, with certified copies available. The fee page prices a certified death certificate and a certified marriage license copy at $10 each, and notes that not everyone may obtain a certified copy, so confirm eligibility first.

An heir selling a parent's house would normally gather the death certificate, the vesting deed and certified copies of recorded papers touching the land; those copies run $5 for page one and $2 for each page after. If an estate is involved, ask the Carteret County Clerk of Superior Court what the estate file requires.

The office describes itself as a recording office, so it gives no legal advice, supplies no legal forms and will not explain the legal effect of an instrument. Use an attorney for drafting.

How big is the Carteret County housing market?

The land area is 507.60 square miles, and the Census estimate for July 2025 is 70,469 people, up 4.1% from the 2020 base. The Census counts 54,293 housing units against 31,977 households for 2020-2024, so the county has well over 20,000 more homes than households.

  • The median owned home was worth $333,300 over 2020-2024, and owners occupy 74.7% of units.
  • Median gross rent: $1,108.
  • Median household income: $72,322.
  • Residents 65 and over: 30.1%.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 471.
  • Persons per household: 2.13; households 31,977.

Those figures are from the Census QuickFacts page. If you own here but live elsewhere, documents can be mailed to the Beaufort address above, and the county's online database lets you check the record from a distance.

More questions about Carteret County, NC Register of Deeds

Will Carteret County charge me to file a release after I pay off my mortgage?

No. The county's fee page lists satisfaction instruments at no fee per statute, so paying off a loan does not cost anything to record the release.

What does a standard Carteret County deed cost to file?

Expect $26 through page 15, then $4 per added page. A deed that breaks the layout standards adds $25, and a document that bundles several instruments adds $10.

How can I pay for recording at the Carteret County register of deeds?

Bring cash, a card, a money order or a cashier's check. Mail can be sent to 302 Courthouse Square, Beaufort, NC 28516.

Can I view Carteret County deeds online?

Yes. The county says land records can be viewed and printed from its Register of Deeds Online Database. Books 301 through 514 are on aperture cards, so call the office about cancellation details for those older records.

What is the Carteret County transfer tax rate?

The county lists it as $2 per $1000.00 of the sales price, the same as the state's $1.00 per $500.00, and the seller pays it before filing.

Catawba County by the numbers

What does the Catawba County Register of Deeds record?

The Catawba County Register of Deeds records and keeps deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions, powers of attorney, plats, easements, rights of way, assumed names and similar land documents. It also holds birth and death records, issues marriage licenses and administers notary oaths. Its land records start in 1842, the year the county was carved out of Lincoln County, which keeps anything older.

The counter is open for recording and for viewing filed records on weekdays from eight in the morning to five in the afternoon, holidays excepted. Its phone number is (828) 465-1573. Indexes and images go online once a document is recorded, with the caution that they have not been verified. The county says recorded documents are scanned within one business day.

Voters elect the register. The office may not prepare documents or advise on legal questions, so a deed needs an attorney's drafting. Wills and divorces belong to the clerk of superior court, who the county lists at (828) 695-6100.

How do you record a deed in Catawba County?

A paper filer delivers the signed, acknowledged deed with payment, while an electronic filer goes through one of the county's two eRecording companies: Simplifile (800-460-5657) or CSC (866-652-0111). The filer completes a memorandum of understanding with the company before the first submission. For 2023 the county counted 16,868 eRecorded real estate documents, a 74 percent average.

Paper filers should check a short list before the trip:

  • A deed cannot be accepted without the buyer's present mailing address on it.
  • A map or real estate instrument must name and address whoever receives it after recording.
  • Anything you want mailed back requires a stamped, addressed envelope big enough to hold it.
  • The instrument must meet the state's recording standards, and the office says it uses Times New Roman as its standard font.
  • A cover sheet may be required for some documents, so ask first if you are unsure.

Timing matters because of G.S. 47-18: until a conveyance is registered where the land lies, it does not protect against lien creditors or later buyers who paid value, and priority runs by registration time. Ask your closing attorney when the deed will reach the register.

Which fees and excise tax apply to a Catawba County deed?

Recording fees are set by state statute and the county adds a few surcharges that show up in its own fee notes. The excise tax is separate, and the seller pays it. The table collects the figures as printed by the county and by G.S. 161-10.

Catawba County recording charges as printed in the county notes and state statute
ItemAs printedSource
General instruments, a deed among them$26.00 covers pages 1 to 15; each page beyond adds $4.00G.S. 161-10
Loan security instruments (mortgage, deed of trust)$64.00 covers pages 1 to 35; each page beyond adds $4.00G.S. 161-10
Subdivision plat$21.00 for every sheetG.S. 161-10
Paper that fails the state's format standards$25.00 extraCounty fee page, citing G.S. 161-10(a)(18a)
Assignment citing several deeds of trust$10 each after the first one citedCounty recording fees page
Instrument naming over 20 parties$2 for every extra party indexedCounty recording fees page
Photocopy of a recorded deed$.25 a pageCounty how-do-I page
Photocopy of a recorded plat$2.00 flatCounty how-do-I page
Conveyance excise tax$1.00 per $500 of value, rounded up by fractionStatute section 105-228.30

In the county's wording the tax is $2.00 per $1,000 of price, owed by the seller, and no stamp is due when nothing was paid for the transfer. Satisfactions of deeds of trust record free. Payment can be cash, a business check or a debit or credit card.

By statute, half the proceeds stay in the county general fund and half, net of refunds and an allowance, reach the state.

Where do you look up a Catawba County property by address?

The register's records describe land by legal description, not by street address, so an address search belongs with Tax Mapping. Three county numbers cover most seller questions:

  • Register of Deeds, (828) 465-1573, for recording, copies and the index.
  • Tax Mapping, (828) 465-8420, for matching an address to a parcel.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, (828) 695-6100, for wills and divorce records.

Mapping staff or the online real estate maps will do the address lookup. Keep in mind that the GIS map is not a legal or binding map. Then take the parcel details to the Register of Deeds online deed search to read the chain of title.

The office notes that it cannot correct a missing item, error or misspelling on an original recorded document under G.S. 132-3, so ask the office what it can do and expect to need an attorney for a correction. If a deed is lost, the office can issue a certified copy bearing its seal, which carries the same weight as the original.

The county's position is that the recording of a deed, more than the paper itself, is the main evidence of ownership. A seller who inherited or bought long ago should look for the vesting deed in the index before listing.

How does recording tie to selling a Catawba County house?

A financed sale in Catawba County produces up to three recordings: the deed into the buyer, the buyer's deed of trust, and a satisfaction of the seller's old loan, which records without charge. Options, contracts to convey and leases longer than three years need registration too if they are to bind later purchasers.

Chapter 47H governs contract-for-deed sales of one to four family homes in which the seller holds title through five or more payments. The seller must record the contract, or a memorandum of it, within five business days, and the buyer's right to cancel lasts through the third business day. A seller who used that structure should check the Catawba County index for the memorandum.

Property tax runs alongside recording. The county's tax office, not the register, can state what is owed on the parcel, and any deferred circuit breaker balance comes due on transfer.

What is Catawba County like for a house seller?

The county measures 413 square miles, 399 of them land, in the Blue Ridge foothills. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate counts 170,172 people and 77,827 housing units. Owned homes carried a $241,600 median value in 2020-2024, and owners live in 72.2 percent of homes.

Catawba County recorded 1,944 building permits in 2025, and its median household income is $67,864. An old tract's chain of title can run back past 1842, and the county says pre-1842 records are held in Lincoln County.

More questions about Catawba County, NC Register of Deeds

Where is the Catawba County Register of Deeds?

The county site lists weekday recording hours from 8 to 5, holidays excepted, and a phone line of (828) 465-1573. Ask for the office's current street address when you call. eRecording is also available.

What are the charges for filing a deed with Catawba County?

The fee table on this page lists each charge, drawn from the county's fee notes and G.S. 161-10. Page count drives the base fee, a $25.00 surcharge applies if the format rules are missed, and the seller separately owes the conveyance excise tax. Call (828) 465-1573 to confirm a total before you send a check.

Can Catawba County record a deed electronically?

Yes. The county accepts all document types for eRecording through Simplifile (800-460-5657) and CSC (866-652-0111). The submitter completes a memorandum of understanding with the provider first. The county counted 16,868 eRecorded real estate documents in 2023.

Does the Register of Deeds prepare deeds in Catawba County?

No. State law bars the office from preparing legal documents or giving legal advice, so you need an attorney to draft or correct a deed. The office can show you how to use the indexes and can issue certified copies of recorded deeds at $.25 per page.

Who pays the deed excise tax in Catawba County?

The grantor, meaning the seller, settles it with the register before the deed is accepted for recording. The tax runs $1.00 on every $500 of consideration, with part of $500 counted as a full unit. Where nothing was exchanged, the county says no stamp applies.

Chatham County by the numbers

Where is the Chatham County Register of Deeds?

You will find it inside the Courthouse Annex, 12 East Street, Pittsboro, ground-level wing, facing the traffic circle where the historic Superior Courthouse stands. Parking is behind the annex and is reached from Chatham Street, which is also US 15/501 South, just past the circle. From the lot, walk to the wide stairwell opening in the middle of the building, skip the stairs, and take the passage on the left to the end of the building nearest the BP station.

Letters go to P.O. Box 756, Pittsboro, NC 27312, while couriers use the East Street address. The main number is 919-542-8235.

Chatham posts three clocks, and a closing that slips past the earlier ones will wait until the next business day.

  • Counter open: eight in the morning until five in the evening on weekdays.
  • Paper documents accepted for recording until 4:30 p.m.
  • Electronic submissions accepted from 8:00 a.m. through 4:00 p.m.

The office closes on state holidays. Its 2026 closing list ends with Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, then December 24, 25 and 28.

What does Chatham charge to put a deed on record?

The base price for a deed is $26.00 covering 15 pages, then $4.00 per extra page, and the office notes a $2 verification fee is folded into that amount. A mortgage-style deed of trust is $64 for the first 35 pages with the same $4 per extra page. The table below repeats the real estate items from the county's own fee list.

Land record charges listed on the Pittsboro office's fee page
ItemFee
General instrument$26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page
Deed$26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page
Deed of trust$64 through page 35, then $4 a page
Release of a deed of trustNo fee
Plat of land$21.00
Certified copy of land records$5 first page, $2 each added page
Uncertified copies of records25 cents per page
Extra instrument inside one document$10.00 each

These match the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10, which also makes a nonstandard document cost $25.00 extra. The county lists a uniform commercial code filing at $38.00 for one or two pages. Fees are collected before a document is filed.

Can a Chatham County deed be filed online?

Electronic filing runs through two vendors, Simplifile and CSC, and the office takes those submissions Monday to Friday until 4:00 p.m. The office says it now e-records plats as well. Closing attorneys and title companies can submit through those vendors, which means a seller often never carries the deed to the office.

CSC lists erecording@cscglobal.com and 1-866-652-0111 for questions about its service. A paper filing needs original documents, and the county notes that the register of deeds is a depository of records, not a creator of documents or a fixer of mistakes. Staff cannot draft or correct a deed for you.

Online searching is separate. The county's remote access site, chathamncrod.org, lets you look up recorded deeds, and the same office offers an e-mail alert if a document with a chosen name is ever filed. An owner worried about deed fraud can sign up through that site.

What formatting rules can get a Chatham County deed rejected?

Anything filed after July 1, 2002 must follow the page layout in G.S. 161-14(b), which the county reprints. A document that misses a rule still gets recorded, but the office first collects a $25.00 nonstandard fee, so clean formatting saves money. The county lists these requirements.

  • Letter or legal sheets only.
  • Leave three empty inches above the first line of page one; every other edge needs a quarter inch of white space.
  • Dark print on white stock, one side only, with type no smaller than 9 points.
  • The kind of instrument (for example, warranty deed) labeled under the blank top band.
  • A prepared-by line on the first page of any deed or deed of trust, kept out of the margin zones.
  • Who gets the original back, with a mailing address, on the first page of every paper filing.

Pen is acceptable for blanks on printed forms and for corrections.

How does the deed excise tax work in Chatham County?

Each $500 of price, or fraction of $500, carries $1.00 of tax, which the seller hands to the office ahead of recording under G.S. 105-228.30. The county general fund keeps half and the state revenue department receives the balance. The closing attorney deducts it from the seller's proceeds and sends it with the recording package, so look for it as a line on the settlement statement.

Order of filing matters. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance gives no shield against later buyers or lien creditors until the register of deeds in the land's county has it on file; priority follows the clock time of filing. In practice, a buyer's lender wants the deed logged before any other filing against the house.

Local numbers show what flows through this counter. QuickFacts lists 38,294 housing units for mid-2025 and 517 building permits in 2025, plus a $446,200 median home value for 2020 to 2024 (Census QuickFacts). With values that high, the per-$500 tax is a bigger line item on a Chatham closing than in many counties, and sellers should budget for it before listing.

What other services does the Chatham County Register of Deeds offer?

Beyond land records, the office is the keeper of births, deaths and marriages for the county, and it files notary oaths and assumed-name records. Marriage licenses and notary oaths are by appointment only, and the line for appointments is the same 919-542-8235.

Certified copies of birth and death records are $10.00 each, and a marriage license is $60.00. These records matter to sellers more often than people expect: an heir selling a parent's house may need a certified death certificate to give the title company, and a divorce or marriage can change who must sign the deed. Request certified copies early, because the office cannot hand over a record to someone who is not eligible under state law.

The register of deeds also runs an alert service for document fraud, covered above, which is useful to any owner who is about to sell and wants to know if anything unexpected is filed under the family name.

What should a Chatham County seller do before the deed is recorded?

Settle property tax, gather the paperwork and let the closing office handle recording. Chatham reappraises on a four-year cycle and kept its county rate at 60 cents per $100 for fiscal year 2026-27, so the tax figure on a settlement statement may differ from the older bill you remember. Our Chatham County property tax guide covers the offices, appeals and relief programs.

A seller with a deed of trust should ask the lender for a payoff and expect a cancellation to be recorded afterward at no fee. A seller with a plat issue, an old easement or a missing signature on an inherited parcel should raise it early, since the register of deeds will not repair a defect.Ask a North Carolina attorney how to fix a title defect before you list.

More questions about Chatham County, NC Register of Deeds

What number reaches the Pittsboro recording desk?

Dial 919-542-8235. Staff there can answer questions about filing a package, and the physical office is at 12 East Street with a mailing box at P.O. Box 756.

What is the latest I can bring a paper deed to the Chatham counter?

Half past four, on business days. Electronic filings cut off earlier, at four, and holidays on the state calendar mean no recording at all.

What is the fee for an ordinary deed?

Budget $26.00 for a short deed of up to fifteen pages, with $4.00 more for every added page. The excise tax paid by the seller is a different charge.

What if my deed ignores the layout rules?

The office will accept it and add $25.00 for a nonstandard document under G.S. 161-10(a)(19). Fix the top band and print dark on white before you submit.

Which electronic vendors does Chatham work with?

Simplifile and CSC. Both feed the register of deeds on weekdays up to 4:00 p.m., and plats can now go in electronically too.

Which office files Cherokee County deeds?

Deeds for Cherokee County land are recorded at the Register of Deeds in Murphy, in Suite 126-A at 75 Peachtree Street. The posted phone is 828-837-2613, and land records are taken between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Besides deeds, the same counter files survey plats, UCC statements and soldier discharges, certifies notaries and keeps the county's birth, death and marriage records.

According to Census QuickFacts, 30,830 people lived in Cherokee County as of mid-2025, across 455.54 land square miles, with 2020 density at 63.2 people per square mile. The county has 19,158 housing units, with an owner-occupied rate of 83.7%. Accommodation and food services sales were listed at 317,976 thousand dollars for 2022.

One in three residents (33.7%) is 65 or older, and the county saw 239 building permits in 2025. Older owners may hold property tax relief that changes when a house sells, which is covered below.

What does the Cherokee County Register of Deeds charge?

Fifteen pages of a deed cost $26 and thirty-five pages of a deed of trust cost $64, with $4 charged on each page beyond those counts. The office's posted schedule follows, in the office's own wording.

Murphy office charges for recording, copies and related services

Deeds, all documents except deeds of trust$26 through page 15, $4 per page after

The county page notes that plats filed since October 1991 must be on mylar transparent plastic in 18 by 24, 21 by 30 or 24 by 36 inch sizes. Certified birth, death and marriage certificates are $10 each. The recording numbers line up with the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10, and that statute lists no fee for recording a cancellation of a deed of trust.

How do deed stamps work in Cherokee County?

Stamps appear on the county page at $2 per $1,000 of purchase price, matching the statute's $1.00 for each $500 slice. G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor responsible, with payment due to the register ahead of filing. One half supports the county's general fund and the other half goes to Raleigh.

What this means for a seller in the county:

  • Look for the stamp tax among the seller's charges.
  • The statute counts every $500 of price or fractional part of $500, so an uneven price rounds up to the next step.
  • Options, contracts to convey and leases longer than three years only bind later purchasers and lien creditors after registration where the land sits, per G.S. 47-18.

Where can I see Cherokee County tax and deed information?

The county's interactive tax viewer shows tax amounts from 2008 forward and refreshes itself each morning at 6 a.m., so a payment shows up the next day. First comes a disclaimer: the data was built for the county's internal use from recorded deeds and plats, and users are told to verify against the public records.

Questions about the data go to the Cherokee County Appraisal Office at 828-835-3296. That office is the one to call about a value, a parcel record or a mismatch between the tax viewer and a deed. For the deed itself, the register of deeds in Murphy keeps the original recorded copy, and a certified copy costs $5 for the first page and $2 for each page after that.

Older, disabled and veteran owners file relief requests locally with the county assessor. For 2026, owners 65 or older (or disabled) with income no higher than $38,800 can exclude the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value, while the disabled veteran exclusion shields the first $45,000. Owners apply on form AV-9, and filings are taken up to June 1 ahead of the tax year. A seller already receiving one of these benefits should ask the Appraisal Office how a sale affects it. The statutes are G.S. 105-277.1 and G.S. 105-277.1C.

What else does the Cherokee County register handle for homeowners?

The office also keeps vital records and issues marriage licenses, and a few of those charges come up around a home sale. A death certificate may be needed by heirs, a marriage license or certificate can bear on who signs a deed, and a notary appointment is available for $10.

  • Certified birth, death and marriage certificates are $10 each; the county directs requests through its vital records portal.
  • A marriage license is $60.
  • Notary appointments are $10 each.
  • Copies of any record are $0.10 apiece.

These items follow the county's price list. If heirs need a certified certificate, order it early so the title company has it when the file is reviewed.

What should a Cherokee County seller prepare before recording?

Sort out the tax bill, the payoff and the title work first, then let the closing attorney file. Bills fall due September 1 and start accruing interest on January 6 under G.S. 105-360. Because the lien rides with the parcel from the listing date, the closing office usually pays the current bill out of the sale money.

These steps help a sale go smoothly.

  • Confirm every owner on the chain of title, including heirs on an inherited house.
  • Ask a surveyor about plats if the lot lines are unclear, since a plat is a separate $21 filing.
  • Collect payoff letters for any deed of trust; the register records the release at no charge.
  • Pull your own vesting deed so the legal description in the new deed matches it word for word.

A register of deeds records documents but does not draft them, so hire a North Carolina attorney for the deed. If repairs, liens or disagreeing heirs have stalled a sale, a cash purchase avoids a lender's schedule; our North Carolina page explains that route.

What do Cherokee County's housing figures show?

From 2020 to 2024 the typical owned home was valued at $232,300, the typical household earned $53,628 and gross rent had a middle point of $813, all per Census QuickFacts. The poverty rate is 15.4%. The county counts 13,241 households of 2.20 people each, and 89.5% of residents kept the same address from the prior year.

Those figures point to settled owners and moderate prices. Owners pay a median of $1,242 a month with a mortgage and $376 without. For a seller, the $2 per $1,000 stamp is a modest charge beside the equity in a typical house, although it grows with the price.

The same QuickFacts table counts 2,522 veterans for 2020 to 2024, which is relevant because the disabled veteran exclusion has no age or income cap. Commutes average 25.2 minutes, and 49.2% of people 16 or older are working or looking for work.

More questions about Cherokee County, NC Register of Deeds

Where is the Cherokee County register's office?

It is at 75 Peachtree Street, Suite 126-A, Murphy, NC 28906. Call 828-837-2613 to reach the register, and bring land records in by 4:30 p.m.

What does recording a Cherokee County deed cost?

The county lists $26 for a deed up to 15 pages, then $4 a page. Deeds of trust are $64 up to 35 pages, and a plat filing is $21.

What are Cherokee County deed stamps?

The county prints the stamp as $2 for each $1,000 of price, which is the same rate the state writes as $1.00 per $500. Sellers pay it when the deed goes on record.

Who answers questions about a Cherokee County tax value?

The Cherokee County Appraisal Office, at 828-835-3296, takes questions about the parcel data in the county's tax viewer.

Is there a charge for deed copies?

Yes. Ordinary copies run ten cents a page, while a certified document is $5 for page one and $2 per page afterward. Vital record certificates are $10 each.

Where is the Chowan County Register of Deeds?

The Chowan County Register of Deeds works out of the courthouse at 101 S. Broad Street in Edenton, with a mailing box at PO Box 487, Edenton, NC 27932. The office phone is (252) 482-2619 and the fax is (252) 482-3062. Counter hours are eight to five on weekdays.

Its own mission statement calls the office the custodian of vital records and real estate recordings. Its archive of real estate material reaches back to the 1600s, marriage licenses are dated as early as 1868, and birth and death records were not required to be recorded until 1913. For sellers, that depth means a title search here can run through very old deeds.

Census QuickFacts shows 14,082 residents in July 2025 on 172.66 square miles of land, down from 14,793 at the 2010 census and up 2.7% from the 2020 base. There are 7,312 housing units, and permits numbered just 48 for 2025, so most deeds here move existing houses and land.

What must be done before a deed is recorded in Chowan County?

Chowan's pre-recording checklist adds a local land transfer tax, a parcel number and a tax office stop. The recording page spells out each requirement, and the table below follows the office's own order.

Pre-recording checklist from the Edenton office
RequirementWhat the county page says

Tax officeDeed presented with an affidavit of consideration before recording

Every document must also be dated and carry a legal description. Deeds with an attached survey, and other surveys, must be reviewed and signed by the county's review officer before recording.

Does Chowan County have a land transfer tax on top of the state excise tax?

Yes. The county's checklist adds a land transfer tax of 1% of the sale price, citing S.L. 1985-881, alongside the excise tax. The excise tax is the state levy, which the statute (G.S. 105-228.30) writes as $1.00 per $500 and the county writes as $2.00 per $1,000, to be paid by the transferor before the deed goes on record.

Both charges scale with the price. Do not estimate either from memory: ask the register of deeds or your closing attorney for the current figure and for how it is split on your contract. On the checklist, payment of both is a precondition to recording.

The typical Chowan home was worth $235,800 in the 2020 to 2024 survey period, and 70.5% of units are owner-occupied. Median household income was $53,864, and 15.9% of residents were in poverty. Check each tax line on a net sheet before you accept it.

Where do Chowan County deeds go before they reach the register of deeds?

Two county offices touch a deed first. The Land Records/GIS Department approves a parcel identification number for any real estate document with a legal description, including plats, and its review officer signs off on surveys. The department is in the courthouse at 101 S. Broad Street and takes calls at (252) 482-7157.

The Chowan County Tax Office is the second stop, and it is a step many sellers miss. All deeds must be presented there with an affidavit of consideration before the register of deeds will record. The tax office is at 305 W. Freemason Street, Edenton, with a phone number of (252) 482-8486 and a mailing address of PO Box 1030.

A sensible order is below.

  1. Have the deed drafted by an attorney with the drafter's name, the grantee's mailing address and a legal description.
  2. Get the parcel number approved by Land Records/GIS, plus review of any attached survey.
  3. Take the deed and an affidavit of consideration to the tax office.
  4. Pay the recording fee, excise tax and transfer tax at the register of deeds, and record.

A closing attorney normally handles these steps, but a seller who is giving a deed to a family member or buyer without one will need to do them personally.

How does e-recording work in Chowan County?

The Edenton office says it is e-recording satisfactions only, which leaves deeds, deeds of trust and plats to paper filing. A satisfaction is the document that releases a paid-off mortgage or deed of trust, and lenders and title companies can send those electronically. Anything else, including the deed that sells your house, goes in by hand or by mail with the right fee.

The office also takes online orders for certified documents using a debit or credit card. Buyers can choose pickup or mail, and a small processing fee is added at checkout. The same page warns that staff cannot help complete documents or perform a title search, because North Carolina law prohibits the unauthorized practice of law.

As for fees, the schedule comes from G.S. 161-10, which sets $26.00 for a general instrument through 15 pages and $64.00 for a deed of trust through 35, with $4.00 per page past those limits. Chowan's posted fee list controls the exact amount, so confirm by phone before mailing a check.

Which property tax relief programs can affect a Chowan County sale?

Three state programs reduce or defer tax for qualifying owners, and each is claimed with the county assessor rather than the Department of Revenue. QuickFacts shows 29.3% of Chowan's population at 65 or older and 1,177 veterans, so a good number of owners may qualify.

  • Senior or disabled owners can exclude whichever is larger, $25,000 or half of a primary home's appraised value, if 2026 income is at most $38,800.
  • Disabled veterans, and unmarried surviving spouses, get $45,000 of appraised value excluded; the state form says no age or income limit applies.
  • A circuit breaker caps the bill at a share of income and defers the excess as a lien that falls due on a sale or the owner's death.

That deferral is the part that matters at closing: deferred tax for up to three prior years is payable on a disqualifying event, such as a sale. Statutory details are in G.S. 105-277.1B, and the AV-9 application goes to the county tax office.

What should a Chowan County seller know about recording priority and property tax?

An unregistered deed protects little, since G.S. 47-18 binds purchasers and lien creditors only from registration in the land's home county. The earlier registration generally wins, which is why sellers and buyers want the deed filed the same day as closing.

Property taxes are the other practical item. Tax bills come due September 1 and gather interest after January 5 under G.S. 105-360, and the tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date. The Tax Office, reachable at (252) 482-8486, can give you the current balance, the next revaluation year and any relief program on the house.

If you inherited a Chowan house, are behind on payments or want to avoid repairs, our North Carolina page describes a cash sale route.

What number do I call for Chowan deed questions?

Call (252) 482-2619. The courthouse office at 101 S. Broad Street, Edenton, serves the public on weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00.

Does Chowan County e-record deeds?

No, the county page says it is now e-recording satisfactions only. A deed must be mailed or delivered to the Edenton office with the correct fee.

What taxes does Chowan County list for recording a deed?

The checklist lists a land transfer tax of 1% of the sale price and an excise tax of $2.00 per $1,000 or fraction. Both must be paid before the deed is recorded.

Do I have to visit the tax office before recording in Chowan County?

Yes. The register of deeds requires every deed to be presented to the Chowan County Tax Office with an affidavit of consideration first. The tax office is at 305 W. Freemason Street, Edenton.

Can Chowan County staff help me write or fix my deed?

No. Staff cannot help complete documents or do a title search, since doing so would be unauthorized practice of law under North Carolina statutes. Use a North Carolina attorney for drafting.

Where does Clay County keep its deed records, and what is filed there?

The Clay County Register of Deeds is at 261 Courthouse Drive, Suite 2, in Hayesville, and the office phone is 828-389-0087. The deed that passes your house to a buyer is filed in this office's permanent land record.

The office website says the staff records deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names and powers of attorney. Vital records, marriage licenses, military discharges and notary commissions are handled at the same counter. On the land-record side, this is where a buyer's lender or title attorney will confirm that your deed went in correctly.

Know the limit before you walk in. Staff file paper; they do not give legal advice, supply forms, coach you through drafting or explain how a recorded instrument affects your rights. Bring those questions to a lawyer first.

What must a Clay County deed look like on the page?

The county publishes layout rules, and a deed that ignores them costs extra to file. The real estate records page spells them out.

  • Sheets of 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches, with black print on white stock and nothing on the back.
  • Leave three inches empty above the text on page one, with a quarter inch left blank along the remaining edges of that page and all edges of later pages.
  • Nothing smaller than 9-point type. Blanks and corrections may be inked by hand.
  • The document type, such as Deed, stated on page one beneath the empty band.
  • The signer's signature, plus a notary's seal and acknowledgment.
  • For deeds and loan documents, add a "Prepared By" line naming the drafter, the grantee's mailing address and the excise tax noted on the deed itself.

A paper that misses the mark still gets filed, but the clerk first collects a $25.00 non-standard document fee, which the county page ties to G.S. 161-10(a)(19). Fixing margins beforehand avoids it.

What are the recording charges for a Clay County deed?

One statewide schedule applies, so Clay County charges what every other register charges. The table gives each figure as printed, plus the excise line from the Clay County page.

What a Clay County seller pays at the Hayesville counter. Sources: the statutory fee schedule, the excise statute and the county's real estate records page.

The two excise lines state the same rate in different words. Fees are collected up front, so ask the office to total your packet before you go.

Who pays excise tax on a Clay County house sale?

The seller does. The grantor carries it, and the register will not file the deed until it is paid.

Clay County's general fund keeps half. The other half, less refunds and the county's allowance, goes to the state each month. On a settlement statement it shows up under the seller's charges.

Why does the filing order matter to a Clay County seller?

Under G.S. 47-18 a deed gives a buyer no shield against lien creditors or rival purchasers until it is registered where the land sits, and priority follows the time of registration.

Options, contracts to convey, leases longer than three years and rights of first refusal or first offer follow the same rule. If you grant a buyer an option on Clay County land, expect them to record it here.

Seller financing has its own chapter. For a one to four family home sold on a contract for deed, the seller has five business days to record the contract or a memorandum, and the buyer can back out until midnight on the third business day.

How did the 2026 reappraisal change things for Clay County owners?

New real property values arrived in 2026. The tax office appeals page says reappraisals run every eight years and posts the 2026 calendar.

  • Official value notices went out in April 2026.
  • The informal review window ran from April 21 to May 20, 2026.
  • The formal appeal window ran from June 1 to 9 a.m. on August 17, 2026, and has closed.

Those windows have passed, but they show the sequence: review the notice, file a written or in-person appeal, then possibly appear before the board. Questions about how the new value flows into your next bill belong with the tax office, not the register. The collector also bills Town of Hayesville taxes, and the online payment portal lists a 2.25 percent service fee on credit cards, a $4.95 flat debit fee and a $2.00 electronic check fee.

Bills fall due September 1, and a payment made after January 5 picks up interest: 2 percent at first, then three-fourths of a percent for each month starting in February (G.S. 105-360). Ask whoever handles your closing to verify the bill is paid.

How large is the Clay County housing market?

It is small. The Census QuickFacts page shows 12,239 residents (July 2025 estimate) across 214.98 square miles of land area, with 7,868 housing units.

Occupied homes are 81.2 percent owner-held, with a median value of $278,400 and median gross rent of $804 (2020 to 2024 survey years). People aged 65 and up make up 37.4 percent of residents, median household income is $56,971, and the 5,081 households average 2.26 people. The county counts 644 veterans. With so many older owners, inherited houses are a real part of the local market, which is why the next section covers estates.

How does an inherited Clay County house reach the register of deeds?

An heir selling a Clay County house needs a chain of title back to the person who died, and that chain starts with the superior court clerk, not at the register's counter.

G.S. 28A-25-1 lets an heir or creditor collect a small estate by affidavit if personal property net of liens is no more than $20,000 and 30 days have passed. A lone surviving spouse may go up to $30,000 after any spousal allowance. The filing goes to the clerk where the decedent lived and must describe each parcel of land the decedent held. There is no state estate tax for deaths since January 1, 2013, because the statutes were repealed.

When the clerk's paperwork clears the way, the signed deed goes to Suite 2 and is filed at the rates in the table.

How can a Clay County owner watch for a fraudulent filing?

The register's site links to online real estate records and to a fraud-alert notification service for the county. Once you sign up, a new filing under your name triggers a notice.

Check before you list. A filing you never signed, or an old loan paid off but never cancelled, can stall a closing. Satisfactions are recorded free, so ask a lender to file one once a loan is paid.

More questions about Clay County, NC Register of Deeds

Where are Clay County deeds filed?

In Suite 2 at 261 Courthouse Drive, Hayesville, NC 28904, phone 828-389-0087. The deed should follow the office's published margin, type and notary rules.

Will the Hayesville office help me draft a deed?

No. Staff may not practice law, so they cannot draft, complete or explain a deed. Retain a lawyer for the drafting.

What if my deed breaks the layout rules?

It is still filed, after a $25.00 non-standard document fee. Fix the margins, type size and notations first to skip the fee.

Is the deed tax my cost as the seller?

Yes. It is paid before filing, at $1.00 for each $500.00 of price or value, counting any part of $500.00 as a full unit.

Were Clay County values reset in 2026?

The office says all of its information is public except military discharge records. Passports, marriage licenses (by appointment) and certified vital records go through the same counter, so expect a mixed crowd.

Which documents does the Cleveland County office record, and how do I submit them?

It records the paperwork that moves or secures a house, and it takes submissions on paper, by overnight courier or electronically. The land record recordings page lists what the office files.

  • Deeds and deeds of trust
  • Easements and powers of attorney
  • Satisfactions of paid loans
  • Plats, which have been accepted by e-recording since 2019
  • Assumed business name certificates
  • Notary oaths, by appointment only

Electronic submitters use Simplifile, CSC or ePN. If you send an original by courier and include a prepaid return envelope, the recorded document comes back in it, and the office says there is no extra charge to schedule a FedEx pickup. Wills are not recorded here. Those are filed with the Clerk of Court.

What will Cleveland County charge me for filing and copies?

The office's FAQ prices a filing at $26.00 for up to 15 pages and $4.00 for each page beyond that. Mortgage-type documents run on a longer first block, 35 pages for $64.00, under the state fee statute.

  • Copies of deeds in person: $.25 per page.
  • Certified copies: $5.00 for page one and $2.00 for every page after it.
  • Assumed business name certificate: $26.00 to record, plus a $15.00 vendor convenience fee if filed online, for a $41.00 total through the online portal.
  • Transfer tax on a sale: the FAQ gives the rate as $2.00 per thousand dollars of purchase price.

To put a new name on a title, the FAQ tells people to have a new deed drawn and to see an attorney. Staff record it; they do not draft it.

Who covers the transfer tax when a Cleveland County house sells?

The seller does, and the register collects before filing. The state statute prices it at $1.00 per $500.00 of consideration or value, with any leftover fraction counted as a full $500.00, which matches the office's per-thousand wording.

Half of the money stays in the county's general fund. The other half, minus refunds and the county's allowance, moves on to the state. In a closing, the attorney typically takes it out of the seller's proceeds, so a Cleveland County seller sees a deduction rather than a counter bill.

How far back do Cleveland County land records go online?

Verified online records start in 1995, with older material available in an unverified index and as scanned index books. The available land records page lays out the ranges.

Online coverage as printed by the Cleveland County Register of Deeds.
Record setDates covered
Searchable real property index01/03/1995 to present
New unverified searchable index01/01/1945 to 12/31/1994

Two practical notes follow from that page. Entries from 1979 to 1985 can be searched only by name and year, so you must open the document to see the exact recording date. For images before 1960 you need the book and page number, and a book such as 15-A is typed as 15A with no dash. Anything not online can be viewed in the office, and the office offers escrow accounts for faxed or emailed copies for a fee.

What is the recorded deed notice that arrives in Cleveland County mailboxes?

It is a solicitation that looks like a bill, and the register of deeds warns residents not to pay it. The office describes a mailer that asks for $86.00 for a "Property Assessment Profile" with a copy of your deed.

The same documents cost 25 cents per page from the Cleveland County Mapping Office and the Register of Deeds. The office asks anyone who gets the notice to report it to the Consumer Protection Division of the N.C. Department of Justice at 919-716-6000. The office also runs a fraud detection notification service; after signing up, check your spam folder for the confirmation email and confirm it.

If a relative is selling or has inherited a house in the county, pass the warning along.

Where do plats and parcel maps come from in Cleveland County?

The register of deeds keeps recorded plats only. Every other map comes from the Cleveland County Mapping Office at 704-484-4849, and the same office answers parcel questions asked by street address.

Sellers who plan to divide a lot should call the register before filing, because the office points e-recording filers to it for the review officer and administrator signatures that plats require.

What should an heir or a seller-financing seller sort out before the deed reaches Shelby?

Two situations need extra paperwork before the register can act. After a death, G.S. 28A-25-1 lets an heir, creditor or public administrator use an affidavit instead of a full estate, once 30 days have gone by and personal property net of liens is $20,000 or less. The affidavit goes to the court clerk and describes every tract of real property the decedent owned.

A seller who finances a one to four family home through a contract for deed must record the contract, or a memorandum of it, within five business days under Chapter 47H. Those deals give the buyer until midnight on the third business day to cancel. Both tasks finish at the Shelby counter.

What does the housing market in Cleveland County look like?

Owners live in most Cleveland County homes. The Census QuickFacts puts the July 2025 population at 103,325, on 464.25 square miles of land.

Survey data for 2020 to 2024 count 38,850 households, with 70.9 percent in owner-occupied homes valued at a median of $200,000. Gross rent has a median of $914. Building permits numbered 555 in 2025, household income has a median of $58,534, and one resident in five (20.2 percent) is 65 or older.

Which other Cleveland County office matters after the deed is filed?

Tax Administration shares the building at 311 East Marion Street and answers at 704-484-4843. Take questions about the bill on the parcel you just sold to that office.

Bills are due each September 1 and carry interest from January 6 (G.S. 105-360), so make sure your settlement agent knows what has been paid. Recording is a different step, and G.S. 47-18 ranks instruments by who registers first where the parcel sits. Deeds belong at the Shelby counter the day you close.

More questions about Cleveland County, NC Register of Deeds

When can I visit the Cleveland County deed office?

Weekdays, from opening at eight to closing at five, in Room 151 at 311 E. Marion Street, Shelby. Call 704-484-4834 about land records.

Does the Shelby office accept electronic filings?

Yes. The office e-records through Simplifile, CSC and ePN, and it has taken plats electronically since 2019. Overnight courier recordings are also accepted at the Shelby address.

What is the price of filing a deed in Shelby?

The office quotes $26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 for each added page. A sale also carries transfer tax, which the office puts at $2.00 per thousand dollars of the price.

Are wills filed with the Cleveland County deed office?

Columbus County by the numbers

Which Whiteville office records Columbus County deeds, and until when?

Deeds for Columbus County land go to Suite B at 125 Washington Street in Whiteville. Mail goes to PO Box 1086, ZIP 28472. Doors open at 8:30 each weekday morning and close at 5:00 in the afternoon, apart from county holidays.

Plan around the filing cutoff. Intake for recording ends at 4:45 p.m. every day, a quarter hour before closing time. Marriage license applications close even earlier, at 4:30 p.m.

A home seller meets this office at the very end, since the deed that transfers title and the buyer's lender's deed of trust are both filed here. The closing attorney or title office usually carries the paper over, so your part is mostly knowing the cutoff when you read a closing calendar.

What does a Columbus County deed cost to file?

A flat $26.00 covers the first fifteen pages of an ordinary deed, and each page beyond that adds $4.00. The county's fee notice cites G.S. 161-10, the uniform schedule used by every register of deeds in the state.

Fees on the Columbus County notice, quoted as printed

Other instruments (deeds, easements, most agreements)$26.00 buys 15 pages; $4.00 for every page after

  • Filing the release of a paid-off mortgage costs the seller nothing.
  • Plain copies made at the counter or requested by mail run 25 cents a page, and deeds on the office's online system can be viewed at no charge.
  • A notary oath taken at the office carries a $10 fee payable by cash or local check.

How does the excise tax on a Columbus County deed work?

The seller owes it, and the register collects before filing. State law prices the tax at one dollar per $500 of price or value, rounding a partial $500 up (G.S. 105-228.30). The county's own FAQ words the same rate as $2 per thousand dollars of purchase price.

Half of the money goes into the county's general fund and the state revenue department takes the rest. Since the tax follows price, expect a separate line on the settlement statement, and get the number from your closing attorney before signing day.

Register staff cannot quote the tax on a given sale without the deed in hand. Changing names on title takes a fresh deed, filed at the standard $26.00 rate. The office suggests an attorney for drafting and warns that excise tax may also apply.

Can I record or search Columbus County land records online?

Yes. The county accepts electronic recording of every document type except plats, and a list of approved vendors is on the e-recording page of the register's website. Electronic filing lets a closing package reach the office before the 4:45 p.m. cutoff without anyone driving to Whiteville.

The online index is name based. The office says its retrieval system is name based and cannot say who owns a given street address, so every search starts with a person or company rather than a house number. For parcel-by-parcel ownership by address, use the county tax office, which keeps the land records and mapping staff.

  • Search by owner name on the register's public system and open the recorded deed.
  • Compare the legal description on that deed with your tax bill.
  • Check the deed of trust section for any mortgage with no matching satisfaction.
  • Ask the Clerk of Court, not the register, about mechanics liens and judgments. The register's FAQ points those questions to the courthouse.

Why does the recording date matter to a Columbus County seller?

It decides who wins when two claims compete for the same land. A deed, option, lease past three years or right of first refusal protects its holder against lien creditors and paying buyers only from the moment of registration in the land's home county (G.S. 47-18). The earlier registration ranks first.

That rule is why a signed deed alone does not finish a sale. Until the Columbus County register stamps it with a recording time, a later claim could still jump ahead.

Owner financing follows the same logic. Chapter 47H reaches a one to four family home sold on five or more payments while the seller keeps title. Recording falls to the seller, who has five business days to file the contract or a memorandum of it. The buyer also gets a three business day window to back out. Read the whole chapter before choosing that route.

What farmland notice appears on Columbus County land records?

Session Law 2018-113, quoted on the county tax office page, requires land records to warn title researchers when a tract lies within half a mile of a qualifying poultry, swine or dairy farm, within 600 feet of any other qualifying farm, or within half a mile of a voluntary agricultural district.

A buyer's title search may therefore flag your parcel. The statute adds that no cause of action arises from a researcher's failure to report it, and that real estate brokers and appraisers are not liable for omitting it. It is a notice, not a restriction on the sale. With 938.12 square miles of land and roughly 54 people per square mile (Census, 2020), farm neighbors are common, so expect the question and answer it early.

How does Columbus County look in the Census housing data?

Columbus County is a small, rural market. Census estimates put the July 2025 population at 50,487, below the 58,098 counted in 2010, with 23,724 housing units.

  • Typical home value among owners: $146,000 (2020-2024 estimate).
  • Owners live in 71.1% of homes.
  • Median household income: $49,442 in 2024 dollars.
  • Median gross rent: $824 a month.
  • Residents 65 and older: 22.2%.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 55.

With 55 permits in 2025 and a population below its 2010 level, new construction is thin. Price your expectations against the $146,000 median, and ask your closing attorney which county records to pull before you list.

How do property taxes fit into a Columbus County sale?

County tax bills fall due September 1. The tax office takes payment by mail, phone, drop box and at the counter, and online through columbus.webtaxpay.com. Its mailing box is PO Box 1468 in Whiteville.

A bill stays at face value until early January. From January 6 a 2% charge applies through the end of January, and from February 1 three-fourths of one percent is added per month or part of a month (G.S. 105-360). The lien for real property tax attaches as of the date property is listed under G.S. 105-285 (G.S. 105-355), so the seller's bill follows the parcel into the sale.

Get a payoff figure from the tax office ahead of closing and hand it to whoever drafts the settlement statement. The same office lists staff for senior citizen exemptions. The state's homestead relief for seniors and disabled owners is claimed on Form AV-9 at the assessor, so ask for current paperwork.

More questions about Columbus County, NC Register of Deeds

Who files the deed after a Columbus County sale?

The register's office in Whiteville files it. Your closing attorney or title office normally submits the package, either at the counter or through an e-recording vendor, before the 4:45 p.m. intake cutoff.

What does the register charge for a deed here?

A flat $26.00 covers fifteen pages and each page after adds $4.00, according to the county notice. A deed of trust runs $64.00 for 35 pages.

Who owes the deed excise tax on a Columbus County sale?

The seller owes it. The register collects at the counter before filing, at one dollar per $500 of price or value, which the county FAQ words as $2 per thousand dollars.

Can the Register of Deeds look up who owns a certain address?

No. The office says its retrieval system is name based, so a search needs a person or company name. Use the county tax office for address-based parcel records.

Where do I ask about liens and judgments on a Columbus County property?

Ask the Clerk of Court at the courthouse. The Register of Deeds FAQ sends mechanics lien and judgment questions there, and also check recorded deeds of trust for any unreleased mortgage.

Where do deeds get recorded in Craven County, NC?

The county's own page says the register is one of three county-wide elected offices created under North Carolina law. Real estate work covers deeds, deeds of trust, plats, maps and any other instrument touching land. The same staff also handle vital records, marriage licenses, assumed business names and military discharge records. The office lists property owners, attorneys, surveyors, lenders and real estate professionals among the people it serves. Its holdings reach back more than three centuries. An old family tract can therefore be traced through the same office that records a current sale.

For a seller, the practical rule is the cutoff. The register's notary page states that the office stops recording at 4:30 p.m. and will not swear in notaries after that time either. Ask your closing office whether a late funding will be filed the next business day.

Who pays the deed excise tax in Craven County?

The seller does. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the transferor pays the register before the deed is filed, at one dollar for every $500 of price or value. The register's fee page lists the same rate.

Your closing attorney will compute the exact dollars. This page prints rates only, and the figure on your own deed may differ if the price is not the full value of what changes hands.

How do I record electronically or search Craven County records?

The register's Real Estate page lists three tools: an e-recording partner page, a public records search, and a page on UCC filings. The site also links a Recordation Notification page in its sidebar, so ask the office what that service covers.

E-recording suits lenders and closing offices that send many documents. If you are a private seller and your closing is handled by an attorney, you will rarely file anything yourself. For UCC filings sent by mail, the UCC page tells filers to make checks payable to Register of Deeds at the Pollock Street address.

Registration fixes priority. G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from an unregistered deed, option, lease over three years or right of first refusal against lien creditors and purchasers for value, and competing claims rank by time of registration.

That is the reason sellers ask for the recording confirmation after funding. A release of an old mortgage works the same way. Satisfactions cost nothing to record here, so confirm that a paid-off loan no longer shows as open on the index.

The state's contract for deed chapter, 47H, adds a recording duty of its own: the seller files the contract or a memorandum inside five business days. A buyer may cancel during a three-business-day window, and forfeiture requires written notice with at least 30 days to cure. Anyone thinking of financing a buyer should start with that chapter.

What should a Craven County seller check before the deed is filed?

A short review of the register's index and fee page before closing can catch problems that otherwise surface after funding. The list below follows the county's own fee categories.

  • Confirm the index shows your vesting deed in the name you are selling under, with a legal description that matches the survey or tax record.
  • Check each deed of trust for a matching satisfaction. Satisfactions are recorded free of charge, so a payoff lender has no fee reason to delay one.
  • Count the pages of the deed. Anything over 15 pages adds $4 per page, and a deed of trust over 35 pages does the same.
  • Ask whether the instrument is non-standard, which the county prices at a $25 fee, or whether several recordings are bundled in one document, which adds $10 for separate indexing.
  • Ask Tax Collection for the current-year payoff so the bill is not left open when ownership changes.

None of this replaces advice from your closing attorney, who will see the full title picture, but it gives you the questions to ask.

What do Census numbers show for Craven County homes?

  • Median gross rent: $1,110.
  • Residents 65 and older: 24.2%.
  • Veterans: 10,968.
  • Building permits in 2025: 553.

Population density runs about 142.5 people per square mile. Eight towns appear on the county's municipality page, from Bridgeton to Vanceboro. Ask the tax office whether a town levy applies to your parcel.

What flood and tax items affect a Craven County sale?

The county's planning department improved its Community Rating System class from 8 to 7, and the county says owners in unincorporated areas now receive a 15% discount on flood insurance premiums, up from 10%. A buyer's insurance agent can confirm what applies to a given address.

Tax bills are separate from the register. Bills are due September 1 and carry no interest through January 5. Before closing, ask the Tax Collection Division (252-636-6605) for a payoff figure, so the bill is settled by the time the deed is filed. Rates for the current year are on the tax pages.

If the home faces tax foreclosure, the county's foreclosure page lists properties for sale and gives the tax collection email for questions. The page notes that those listed properties are not owned by the county, and it also points owners to a state homeowner assistance site for delinquent tax help.

In New Bern, at the register's Pollock Street office. Recording ends at 4:30 p.m., so ask your closing office how a later deed is handled.

Where is the Cumberland County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?

The office sits in Room 114 of the Judge E. Maurice Braswell Cumberland County Courthouse, 117 Dick Street in Fayetteville, and the land records line is 910-678-7775. The office keeps its own website at ccrod.org, where the posted office hours and the yearly holiday schedule live.

Cumberland County's land records reach back to 1754, which the office describes as the official start of the county. Other business at the same counter includes notary oaths and vital records, and retired service members can file discharge papers (DD-214) free of charge.

Why does the filing time on a Fayetteville-area deed matter?

North Carolina gives a buyer no shield against competing claimants until the deed reaches the public record at the local courthouse. When two instruments compete, whichever was registered first generally wins, so the time stamp carries real weight.

A few habits keep a sale clean:

  • Get every signature notarized before the paperwork goes to Dick Street.
  • Pair the deed with payment of both tax and fee.
  • Ask your closing attorney to tell you the exact filing date and time.
  • Save the book and page reference from the recorded copy.

Counter staff will not draft or advise on deeds, so wording questions belong with an attorney.

Which recording charges does the Cumberland County office collect?

The posted schedule dates from October 1, 2016. Filing an ordinary deed starts at $26.00, and a mortgage filing starts at $64.00. The table lists the rest of what the office prints.
