Checks and money orders go out in the office's name, and a re-recording is billed like the original filing.

How is the Cumberland County deed excise tax figured?

The county's recording page states the tax as $2.00 against each $1,000 of price, with any leftover fraction counted as a full unit. The statute words the same rate as $1.00 against each $500. Payment travels with the filing fee, and the figure appears on page one of the deed.

The statute's "transferor," meaning the seller, owes it, and the office collects before it records anything. Revenue is then shared evenly between the county and the state. If the contract price falls between round numbers, have your closing attorney supply the exact amount instead of guessing at the window.

What must a deed show before the Cumberland County office will accept it?

Page one of a North Carolina deed must name whoever drafted it, and it should also give a return address. The office lists these points on its recording requirements page:

  • The draftsman line, usually written "Prepared by" or "Drawn by."
  • A return address block, also on page one.
  • The excise tax or revenue amount on the front of the deed.
  • Paper size, margins, font size and page limits that meet state recording standards.
  • Notarization of the signatures before filing.

Satisfactions and UCC filings are exempt from the formatting rules. A deed that misses the mark is still accepted, with $25.00 added for non-standard format.

How does the Property Notification service protect a Cumberland County owner?

This is a no-cost email alert sent whenever a recorded document lists your name. The office pitches it as a defense against deed fraud and tells owners who see an unauthorized filing to call a real estate attorney.

To enroll, visit ccrod.org, pick Records Search, choose New Property Notification and follow the screens. Each alert lists the name matched, the date, the book and page, and a link to the document. The office says plainly that the alerts are no guarantee against fraud. Owners of a vacant or inherited Fayetteville property may find the alerts useful while the house is empty.

How do Cumberland County deed records tie into the property tax listing?

Tax Administration decides who the listing owner is by reading instruments indexed at the Register of Deeds and at the Clerk of Court's estates division on January 1. The county keeps a permanent listing, so owners report only what changed, such as a deck, an in-ground pool or a remodel. Forms are requested back by January 31.

Send them to Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Division, P.O. Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or drop them at Room 530 of the courthouse. Statewide, the bill is due September 1, interest starts January 6 at two percent, with three-quarters of a percent added for each month from February 1 on. Ask Tax Administration how a mid-year sale is handled on the current bill.

A veteran with a permanent, total, service-connected disability rating may apply to the county assessor for the state exclusion, which removes $45,000 from the appraised value.

How does Cumberland County's housing stock look in the Census data?

The Census Bureau puts Cumberland County at 338,473 people in mid-2025, spread over 146,623 housing units and 652.56 square miles of land. Owners occupy 55.0 percent of the homes counted for 2020 to 2024.

  • Owner-occupied homes sit at a median value of $199,200.
  • Median gross rent is $1,222 a month.
  • The county counts 129,758 households averaging 2.48 people.
  • Veterans number 40,226.
  • Median household income is $61,291, in 2024 dollars.

These QuickFacts numbers cover the whole county and say little about a single street.

What should a Cumberland County seller check ahead of signing?

Begin with the mortgage. Filing a satisfaction of a paid-off loan costs nothing, so a cleared mortgage should end with that document on record. If payments have lapsed, the lender uses a power-of-sale case heard by the clerk of superior court, and once a sale is reported anyone may file an upset bid within ten days, at least five percent above the price and no less than $750.00 higher.

Next, study the title. Pull the last recorded deed, look for liens, and check whether a deed of trust remains open. A house that came through an estate also warrants a look at the clerk's estates division records. A sale that skips repairs may trim the to-do list, though the deed, excise tax and filing fee are still due.

More questions about Cumberland County, NC Register of Deeds

Who pays the deed excise tax when selling a house in Cumberland County?

The seller pays, and the statute calls that party the transferor. It is handed over at the counter before the deed is filed. The county page prints $2.00 against each $1,000 of price, and the statute prints $1.00 against each $500.

What does Cumberland County charge to file a deed?

A regular deed starts at $26.00 and covers fifteen pages, with $4.00 for each page after. A mortgage filing starts at $64.00 and covers thirty-five pages. A satisfaction of a loan carries no charge.

Can the Register of Deeds help me write a deed?

No. The office says state law forbids its staff from advising on legal questions or writing deeds. A deed must be drafted, signed and notarized before it is brought in, and an attorney can answer wording questions.

What is the Property Notification service in Cumberland County?

Yes, it costs nothing: an email reaches you whenever someone files paper carrying your name in Fayetteville. Sign up at ccrod.org under Records Search. The office calls it an early warning, with no guarantee against fraud.

Where do I send a Cumberland County real property listing form?

Mail it to Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Division, P.O. Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or bring it to Room 530 of the courthouse. The county asks for forms by January 31 so changes reach that year's assessment.

Uncertified copies at the office$.25 per page
Returned check$25.00

Copies sent through the mail run $1.00 a page. Mail requests also need a stamped return envelope.

How should a document be formatted for Currituck County recording?

A document that ignores the state's format rules (G.S. 161-14) is still recorded, but the office adds $25.00 for a non-standard document. The notices page spells out the rules:

  • Letter size (8 1/2 by 11) or legal size (8 1/2 by 14) paper.
  • Top margin of three inches on the opening page; half-inch margins elsewhere.
  • Black type or print on white paper, no smaller than 10 point.
  • Text on one side of each page only.
  • A title line naming the kind of instrument, placed first.

Blanks and corrections can be made in pen. Documents should also leave out Social Security numbers, driver license numbers, bank account numbers and similar identifiers unless the law requires them. Anyone can ask in writing that such numbers be removed from the online image of a record, and the county charges nothing for that request.

What is the farm proximity notice on Currituck County land records?

State law (G.S. 106-741) requires every county's land records to carry notice when a tract lies near a qualifying farm, which includes one within half a mile of a poultry, swine or dairy farm. Currituck keeps a file of parcels that may fall within half a mile of farm use property, and the posted file was last updated in February 2019.

For a seller with land away from the beach, the point is simple: buyers and their title searchers may see the notice. The statute says no cause of action arises just because a title searcher failed to report a farm nearby. If you are unsure whether your parcel is listed, ask the Register of Deeds staff to point you to the current file.

What are the 2026 Currituck County property tax rates?

The county-wide 2026 rate is .60 per $100 of valuation, down from .62 for 2025, and the county notes the rate is the same for land, buildings, mobile homes, boats, vehicles and business personal property. Several special districts add to it:

  • Carova Beach Road Service District: .02, shown as .62 combined.
  • Corolla Fire Protection Service District: .08, shown as .68 combined.
  • Knotts Island Fire Protection Service District: .09, shown as .69 combined.
  • Moyock Watershed Service District: .01, shown as .61 combined.
  • Ocean Sands North/Crown Point Stormwater: .255, with listed combinations for properties also in the water and sewer or fire districts.

The page also prints solid waste fees for 2026: $500.00 per dwelling unit on the southern Currituck beaches and $274.00 per dwelling unit on the mainland and northern beaches. A 6 percent occupancy tax is listed, which matters if the house has been a vacation rental. The county's tax office can tell you which districts cover your parcel.

How fast is Currituck County growing, according to the Census?

The 2020 count was 28,100 people; the mid-2025 estimate is 33,158, up 18.0 percent. Owners live in 87.3 percent of the occupied homes. Half of the owner-occupied homes are worth more than $378,800, by the Census median.

  • Land area: 261.91 square miles, or about 107 people per square mile.
  • Housing units: 18,351 (July 2025 estimate).
  • Median household income: $93,511 in 2024 dollars.
  • Residents 65 and over: 20.7 percent.
  • Average commute: 35.5 minutes each way.
  • New-construction permits in 2025: 325.

The office address is in the community of Currituck, and the Census table covers the whole county from Moyock to the northern beaches.

What should a Currituck County seller confirm before closing?

Confirm three things: the recorded owner, any deed of trust still open, and the special districts that tax the parcel. A search of the land records shows recorded deeds and deeds of trust, and a satisfaction recorded for a paid loan carries no fee for the first reference.

Next, have the closing attorney put both transfer taxes on the settlement statement, because the office collects them when the deed is presented. Ask the tax office for the balance on the current bill. Statewide, the due date is September 1 and interest begins January 6, so a fall or winter sale should settle whatever remains on the open bill. Sellers who are behind on a mortgage should know that foreclosure here follows the state's clerk-hearing process, with a ten-day upset bid period after the sale report.

More questions about Currituck County, NC Register of Deeds

When can I visit the Currituck Register of Deeds?

The county footer shows weekdays from 8:00 AM until 5:00 PM, at 153 Courthouse Road. Holidays change the schedule, so confirm before driving over.

Does Currituck County charge a land transfer tax?

Yes. Yes. Besides the state excise stamp tax of $1.00 per $500.00, the county's pages show its own land transfer tax of $1 per $100 of price, counting any fraction.

How much is the Currituck County fee to record a deed of trust?

The county fee page prints $64.00 for a deed of trust or mortgage covering pages one through thirty-five. A satisfaction of a deed of trust is $0.00 for the first reference.

Can the Currituck Register of Deeds do a title search for me?

No. The office says it cannot provide legal advice, prepare documents or perform title searches. Staff explain how to look through the records on your own. A title search for a sale is the job of an attorney or title company.

What was the Currituck County property tax rate for 2026?

The county-wide rate is .60 per $100 of valuation for 2026, with added rates in special districts such as Corolla Fire at .08 and Knotts Island Fire at .09. The county tax page prints the full schedule.

Davidson County by the numbers

Where is the Davidson County Register of Deeds and when does it take recordings?

The office is at 110 West Center Street in Lexington, NC 27292, and mail goes to P.O. Box 464, Lexington, NC 27293. The phone is 336-242-2150 and the fax is 336-238-2318. The building is open weekdays from 8am to 5pm, closed on county holidays, yet the office stops taking recordings at exactly 4:30pm under a rule dating from August 1, 2020.

Its stated mission covers real estate records, vital records and military service records, along with the notary oath. Counter visits get same-day recording and same-day return of vital records, and the office offers a public computer lab and self-serve kiosks for legal searches.

How do I search Davidson County land records?

Real estate searches are done online through the county's deeds search site, and records there are indexed from 1984 to the present. For anything earlier than 1984, the office asks you to contact staff directly.

  • When looking for a satisfaction of a mortgage, search under the document type Release.
  • Judgments are looked up through the Clerk of Courts office instead.
  • Attorneys are encouraged to use an e-record system or submit by mail.
  • Color-coded plats do not upload properly and will not be recorded.

The office also lists answers to common questions on whether an instrument must be notarized, whether you can prepare your own deed and whether you must be present to record.

What is the Davidson County tax certification rule for deeds?

Beginning March 1, 2019, the counter turns away any real property deed lacking a certificate from the Tax Administrator that no overdue tax is attached to the parcel. The county adopted the requirement by commissioner resolution on August 14, 2018, under G.S. 161-31.

An attorney-supervised closing offers a way around the certificate. The deed instead carries a printed line saying a North Carolina attorney prepared it and that any overdue tax will be sent to the collector out of the sale money. Without an attorney, you request a certificate from the Tax Department through its online form, and the county warns that a certificate can take up to two business days. A seller handling the sale without an attorney should file the request well before closing, because an unpaid earlier bill will halt the deed at the window.

What will the Davidson County office charge me to file documents?

Davidson County follows the uniform fees North Carolina sets by statute. The table shows the state schedule alongside two charges the county prints on its own page.

Recording charges that apply at the Davidson County Register of Deeds
ItemAmountWhere it comes from
Instrument in general$26.00 for 15 pages, then $4.00 a pageG.S. 161-10
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for 35 pages, then $4.00 a pageG.S. 161-10
Satisfaction or cancellationNo feeG.S. 161-10
Plat$21.00 per sheetG.S. 161-10
Certified copy$5.00 for page one, $2.00 a page afterG.S. 161-10
Assumed business name filing$26.00Davidson County Register of Deeds page
Card payments3% convenience fee or $1 minimumDavidson County Register of Deeds page

Excise tax on the deed is a separate charge. The statute sets it at one dollar for every $500 of price, or part of $500, and the seller settles it at the counter first.

Does recording protect a Davidson County buyer and seller?

Yes. G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from a deed, option or long lease until it is registered locally, and the order of registration settles who ranks first.

That is why a seller in Lexington, Thomasville, Denton or a rural township should treat recording as the final step and not an afterthought. Get the recorded book and page from your closing attorney, plus proof that the earlier deed of trust was released.

Who owes the property tax bill when a Davidson County house changes hands?

The tax collector bills whoever is the listing owner on January 1, and the county says a sale during the year does not erase the seller's liability for that bill. Closings normally split the bill by date, so read the settlement statement to see whether the buyer's portion was credited.

Sellers who want certainty can ask that the tax collector be paid directly out of closing funds. The tax collector's phone number is 336-242-2180, and the same office handles the tax certifications the Register of Deeds requires. Because a certificate and a recorded deed depend on each other, a seller who clears the tax account first usually avoids a delay at the recording counter.

How big is the Davidson County housing market?

Census estimates for mid-2025 show 180,182 residents, a rise of 6.7 percent since the spring 2020 base, living among 79,412 housing units. The county covers 553.18 square miles, and owners live in 74.4 percent of occupied homes.

  • Home value at the Census median: $219,100.
  • Rent at the median: $901 gross.
  • Monthly cost for owners with a mortgage: $1,355 at the median.
  • Households: 69,846, averaging 2.45 people.
  • Persons 65 and over: 20.8 percent.
  • Permits pulled for new building in 2025: 1,216.

Few people move in a given year, with 92.2 percent in their prior-year home. Those figures describe the whole county, not a single town.

What other records does the Davidson County office handle?

Beyond deeds, the office takes military discharges and assumed business name filings by mail at P.O. Box 464, and sellers who are heirs often need its vital records too. Marriage license applications are online, and the applicant then calls to schedule an appointment. A marriage license is valid for 60 days only.

Funeral homes with escrow accounts send certificate requests by fax, and orders are mailed within 48 hours. Others bring the request with payment and proof of their funeral home status, or mail it with a stamped return envelope. Heirs selling a parent's house usually need a death certificate for the estate file, so ordering a few early saves a second trip.

What should a Davidson County seller do before the deed goes in?

Work through a short list in order:

  • Pull the tax bill for the parcel and see whether anything is delinquent.
  • Decide whether an attorney will close the sale or you will request a tax certificate yourself.
  • Confirm the draftsman line and return address on the deed.
  • Arrange payment of the excise tax and filing fee for the same day.
  • Get the loan payoff and a recorded release of the deed of trust.

If the loan is in default, power-of-sale foreclosure is heard before the clerk of superior court, with ten days to file an upset bid after a sale report. Request a written payoff statement from the lender early.

More questions about Davidson County, NC Register of Deeds

What time does the Davidson County Register of Deeds stop recording?

Recording stops at 4:30pm sharp, even though the office stays open until 5pm Monday through Friday. The county put that rule in place on August 1, 2020.

Why was my Davidson County deed refused for taxes?

Since March 1, 2019, the office accepts a real property deed only with a Tax Administrator certificate showing no delinquent taxes, or under a closing attorney who agrees to pay any delinquent taxes from the proceeds. The certificate can take up to two business days.

How far back do the online Davidson County land records go?

Records are indexed from 1984 to the present. For earlier records, contact the Register of Deeds office at 336-242-2150.

Who pays the excise tax on a Davidson County deed?

The seller does, at the counter, ahead of filing. The statute's rate is one dollar for each $500 of price or part of $500.

Can I record documents by mail in Davidson County?

Military discharges and assumed business name filings can be mailed to P.O. Box 464, Lexington, NC 27293. The assumed business name fee is $26.00, and a stamped return envelope is needed for return.

Duplin County by the numbers

Which Kenansville office accepts Duplin County deeds?

Duplin County deeds are filed at 118 Duplin Street in Kenansville, in the Register of Deeds office, open from 8 am until 5 pm Monday through Friday. Call 910-296-2108 with questions; the fax line is 910-296-2344, and mail can go to Box 970, Kenansville, NC 28349.

The county dates the office to the organization of county government in 1750. Besides deeds, the staff handle the following:

  • Deeds of trust and powers of attorney.
  • Assumed business names and military records.
  • Maps and plats.
  • Notary commissions and marriage licenses.
  • Certified copies of vital records.

Real property records, vital records and maps are searchable online, and the county points visitors to duplinrod.com. The county's recommended 2026-27 budget shows five positions in the office and about $499,896 recommended for it, and it sets aside a small automation and preservation fund, budgeted at $25,000, that draws on part of the fees the office collects.

What does registering a Duplin County deed protect?

A deed protects its holder against outsiders only once it is on the public record. G.S. 47-18 says a deed, a contract to convey, an option, a lease running more than three years, or a first-refusal right cannot defeat lien creditors or paying purchasers until it is registered where the land lies.

If two documents compete, the earlier registration wins. A signed deed that is still unfiled leaves the buyer exposed, so sellers should ask the closing attorney when filing will happen.

Tax-side ownership data lives with Land Records inside the Duplin tax department, so call that office after closing to see when the new owner shows on the account.

What does filing a Duplin County deed cost?

A single schedule governs every county. G.S. 161-10 sets it, and payment comes before filing.

Charges from G.S. 161-10 owed when a document is filed in Duplin County
DocumentCharge printed in the statute
General instrument such as a deed$26.00 covers 15 pages; each added page is $4.00
Deed of trust$64.00 covers 35 pages; each added page is $4.00
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each page after
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo charge

Two add-ons appear in the same statute: $25.00 for a nonstandard document and $10.00 for each extra instrument in one filing. Page count drives the total, so count before mailing.

Who pays the deed stamp tax in Duplin County?

The grantor pays. The statute puts the levy at a dollar per five hundred dollars of consideration, rounding any remainder up, collected at the register's counter ahead of recording.

  • The county general fund receives half.
  • The rest is sent on to the state, minus a 2% collection allowance the county retains.
  • A tract spread over several counties pays where most of its value lies.

Let the closing attorney work out the stamp for your price, since the register takes the tax before accepting the deed.

How do I coordinate a Duplin County deed with the tax office?

The register records the deed; the Duplin County Tax Department at 117 Beasley Street bills the tax. Collections answers at 910-296-2112, and the assessing office at 910-296-2110.

Tax comes due September 1, and interest starts on January 6, so a closing in autumn or winter has a live bill attached to it. On delinquent accounts the tax office sends the file to the county attorney, and foreclosure sales take place on the courthouse steps in Kenansville, where the top bidder leaves a 20% deposit.

Phone Collections for a payoff ahead of closing. If the parcel lies in Calypso, Greenevers, Kenansville, Magnolia, Rose Hill, Teachey, Wallace or Warsaw, the county also collects that town's levy, so the payoff should include it.

What steps get a Duplin County deed recorded?

The register will not file a document until the money is in, so the order of steps matters.

  1. Obtain a payoff from Collections so the year's tax and any back balance are cleared at the table.
  2. Have the deed drawn up and signed.
  3. Pay the deed stamp, then add the page-based fee from the table.
  4. Deliver the document to 118 Duplin Street or mail it to Box 970.
  5. If a lender asks for a certified copy later, expect the statutory per-page charge shown in the table.

With an inherited house, settle who may sign for the estate before anything is drafted. The register files the paper without ruling on that, so talk to an attorney and the court clerk before drafting.

Do owner-financed sales get recorded in Duplin County?

Yes, and Chapter 47H adds rules. It reaches written agreements with five or more payments after the down payment, where the seller keeps title, on one-to-four family dwellings or manufactured homes priced at $5,000 or more.

  • Paper, signatures and an acknowledgment are all required.
  • The buyer may rescind up to midnight ending the third business day after execution or delivery.
  • Five business days is the seller's window to record the contract itself or a short memorandum of it.
  • A forfeiture begins with a written default notice giving at least 30 days to cure.

A seller who forgets to record loses the protection described above, so put it on the closing checklist.

Which Duplin County towns and roads do these deeds cover?

The register serves a county of about 819 square miles, bordered by Wayne, Lenoir, Jones, Onslow, Pender and Sampson counties. Kenansville, the county seat, sits roughly in the middle, where NC 24, NC 11 and NC 50 meet, and Interstate 40 and US 117 run through the wider county.

Beulaville, Calypso, Faison, Greenevers, Magnolia, Rose Hill, Teachey, Wallace and Warsaw are the other municipalities the county names. Conveyances of homes in any of these places, or of the farmland between them, all land in the same Kenansville office. The county's own budget message calls Duplin a rural county leaning on agriculture and industry, with little retail growth.

How do Duplin County tax rates and revaluation shape a sale?

A deed transfers the house, but the tax bill moves with the calendar. Duplin's county rate in the recommended 2026-27 budget is 58 cents per $100, and fire districts add their own rates. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2025, and the next is set for January 1, 2030.

The 2025 revaluation lifted the county tax base by about 25%, and the county reported reaching roughly 98 percent of market value. Sellers can therefore expect the assessed value on the bill to sit near market value, which matters when a buyer's lender asks about the tax load. The tax office reported 42,374 nonexempt parcels as of January 2026.

What do Duplin County housing numbers look like?

Census QuickFacts puts Duplin at 51,571 people and 24,235 housing units in July 2025, with owners in 70.3% of homes, spread over 814.72 square miles of land.

Median owner-occupied value was $137,400 for 2020-2024; median rent was $865 and median household income $55,148. Permits for new building totaled 127 in 2025.

More questions about Duplin County, NC Register of Deeds

What hours does the Duplin County Register of Deeds keep?

Staff are on site weekdays, 8 am to 5 pm, at 118 Duplin Street; the number is 910-296-2108.

What will recording my Duplin County deed cost?

The statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10 starts at $26.00 for a short deed and $64.00 for a deed of trust, with $4.00 more for each page beyond the included count.

Who is responsible for the excise tax on a Duplin County sale?

The seller does, at the register's counter before recording, one dollar per five hundred dollars of value.

Are Duplin County deeds searchable online?

Yes. The county says most public records, including real property, vital records and maps, can be searched through the register's website at duplinrod.com.

Does recording the deed clear the Duplin County property tax bill?

No. Tax is billed and collected by the Duplin County Tax Department and is due each September 1, so request a payoff from Collections at 910-296-2112 before closing.

Where is the Durham County deed counter and when is it open?

By Census estimate Durham County had 347,240 residents in mid 2025, on 286.53 square miles of land. Many sellers never see the counter. A law firm or title agent submits the signed deed and gets it back stamped. Your leverage sits in the document itself, so learn the office's rules before you sign.

What fees does Durham County print for filing a deed?

A regular deed runs $26.00 when it has 15 pages or fewer, and $4 more for each page beyond that. Mortgages sit on a separate line, and filing the release of one costs nothing.

Every county uses the same scale, which comes from G.S. 161-10, and the money is collected at the counter.

How is the Durham County deed transfer tax figured?

North Carolina taxes each $500 of price or value at $1, and a leftover slice under $500 counts as a full unit. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the seller settles it at the register's office before the deed goes on file.

The proceeds split down the middle. Durham County keeps one half for its general fund, and the other half goes to the state in monthly remittances. The amount appears on your settlement statement, where you can compare it with the contract price.

  • Because the seller carries this cost, factor it into any offer comparison.
  • Paying off a deed of trust at closing adds no filing charge for the release.
  • The statute measures the tax on consideration or value, so the deed's stated price matters.

Can a Durham County deed be sent in over the internet?

Yes, through any of four vendors the county names. A deed that arrives before 4:45 pm is processed and sent back the same business day, and an individual who wants an account contacts a vendor directly.

  • Simplifile
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • ePN, the eRecording Partners Network
  • CSC, the Corporation Service Company

Title agents often hold accounts already, which lets a Durham closing finish in one day. A seller signing outside a closing can bring the original to the counter in person.

Which format rules must a printed Durham deed meet?

The county's Document Recording Standards page restates G.S. 161-14(b). A paper that breaks a rule still gets filed once the $25.00 surcharge is paid. Print on white letter or legal paper, one side only, and name the instrument type at the head of page one. Leave three inches of blank room above the text on that first page, keep half inch margins on every other edge, and use type of 9 points or bigger. Plat maps measure 18 by 24, and pen is allowed for blanks and corrections.

When tiny print is the only flaw, the registrar can waive the surcharge if the page is legible.

Why does filing the deed protect a Durham County seller and buyer?

Filing settles who stands first. Per G.S. 47-18, a deed cannot beat a lien creditor or a buyer who gave value until it is registered where the land sits, and between rival papers the earlier registration time prevails.

Staff index what they receive and cannot repair a recorded paper. The standards page names misspelled names, defective legal descriptions and wrong parcel numbers as errors outside its power. An indexing slip is reported by email, and the office answers with an Administrative Notice linked to the original entry. Proofread first.

The county also runs a Recording Notification Service that emails citizens when a document is recorded in their name, a handy guard against property fraud on a vacant house.

Who collects Durham County property tax, and how does it touch a sale?

Property tax belongs to another office. Durham County Tax Administration runs it from 201 East Main Street, 3rd Floor (919-560-0300), and the county's latest reappraisal of real property took effect January 1, 2025.

Each year's bill is mailed to whoever owned the parcel on January 1, and the county suggests passing a misdirected bill to the new owner. Get the amount owed from the tax collector ahead of closing so the settlement agent can clear it. Our Durham, NC property tax guide covers due dates and relief programs.

How can I search recorded Durham County documents before I sell?

The county runs an Online Public Records Search, described as a database of recorded real estate and business documents. Looking up your own parcel before listing shows the deeds, deeds of trust and releases in the chain, so you can confirm an old mortgage shows as released.

That check suits inherited houses and owners who paid off a loan years ago, and a satisfaction is free to file. A certified copy of any recorded paper costs $5.00 for the first page and $2 for each added page.

The office handles more than land records. Its own description lists assumed business names, corporate and partnership certificates, military records, notaries and oaths, plats and vital records such as birth, marriage and death certificates. The fee schedule prices a marriage license at $60.00 and a certified birth or death copy at $10.00.

How big is the Durham County housing market?

Census QuickFacts for the county hints at how much paper this office sees.

  • Housing stock of 164,222 units in the July 2025 estimate, with 141,847 households counted in the five year survey.
  • Homeownership rate of 55.5%, with owner-occupied homes valued at a median $389,400.
  • Typical rent of $1,508 and typical household income of $82,316.
  • 4,772 building permits during 2025.
  • Population growth of 6.9% since the April 2020 estimates base, and 1,133.7 people per square mile at the 2020 count.

Because the transfer tax follows the price, a higher median value means a bigger tax line on the closing statement. Compare any offer against your net proceeds line by line, and request an itemized estimate from the settlement agent early.

More questions about Durham County, NC Register of Deeds

Who pays the Durham County excise tax at a sale?

The seller. State law has the transferor pay it to the register of deeds before the deed is filed, at $1 for each $500 of price or leftover fraction. Half stays with Durham County and half goes to the state.

Does Durham County charge to file a mortgage payoff?

No. The county fee schedule shows no fee for a satisfaction, so releasing a deed of trust at closing costs nothing at the register of deeds.

What if my deed is printed in tiny type?

The office can still file it. Missing a layout rule triggers a $25.00 nonstandard surcharge, though the registrar may skip it when the only flaw is print under 9 points and the page reads clearly.

Can a homeowner e-record a deed alone in Durham County?

Usually through a vendor. The county names Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, ePN and CSC, and each sets up its own account. A submission received by 4:45 pm comes back the same business day.

How do I correct a misspelled name on a Durham County deed?

The office cannot change it, since it records and indexes documents as presented. Ask the closing attorney how to correct the deed itself, and email the office only for an indexing error, which it answers with an Administrative Notice.

Edgecombe County by the numbers

How do I contact the Edgecombe County Register of Deeds?

This office keeps the county's land records along with births, deaths, marriages, military discharges, notary files and maps. The county page lists (252) 641-7924, so phone ahead for counter hours and the street address.

The office says three state bodies govern it: the Legislature, the Secretary of State and North Carolina Vital Records. Voters elect each county's register every two years under G.S. 161-1. Tarboro is the county seat in a rural county, roughly an hour east of Raleigh, that the county describes as built on farming with some advanced manufacturing.

When you sell an Edgecombe County house, your signed deed lands here, usually sent by the closing attorney. The next sections cover the charges and local quirks.

What price list does the Edgecombe register of deeds follow?

The office lists $26.00 for a deed of up to 15 pages and $4.00 per later page, with its excise tax line printed as $1.00 per $500.00. The table below follows the office's fee schedule PDF.

Edgecombe County register of deeds fee schedule, reproduced from the county PDF
ServiceAmount

Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 first 35 pages; $4.00 per page past 35

Satisfaction of a mortgageNo fee

The sheet promises same day processing of filings and requests, and asks mail customers to include a stamped, self addressed return envelope.

Why does Edgecombe County ask for a tax certification on deeds?

A county resolution requires every deed to carry the Tax Collector's certification before recording, per the fee schedule, with one way around it. The deed can instead bear a statement that a licensed North Carolina attorney prepared it and that the closing attorney will deliver any delinquent taxes to the county tax collector from the closing proceeds.

An attorney drafting your deed can add that line. If you prepare a deed yourself, stop at the Tax Collector first and request the certification.

  • Attorney route: the preparer statement satisfies the resolution, and back taxes come out of your proceeds.
  • Do it yourself route: obtain the certification before bringing the deed to the register.

Can an Edgecombe County deed be sent in electronically?

Yes. The county's E-Recording page names Simplifile as the vendor and also points to CSC eRecording Solutions. Law firms and title agents with an account can transmit the deed without a courier.

A seller with no account should ask the closing attorney to file it. Paper filings follow the state filing standards that the Real Estate page posts as a PDF, next to an Assumed Name form and property check instructions.

What must never appear in a document I submit for recording?

Leave out Social Security, taxpayer ID, driver's license, state ID, passport, bank account, credit card and debit card numbers, plus PINs and passwords. The county's notice cites G.S. 132-1.10(g)(1) and permits such a number only when a law or court order demands it, or when only the last four digits remain.

Filed documents join the official county records, so read yours before signing and ask the preparer to strip anything sensitive.

How does a deed recording affect farm or timber land here?

The county treats the recording date as the transfer date for Present Use Value purposes. A buyer who wants land to stay in the use value program has 60 days from that date to file a new application.

The program page also says the new owner takes on deferred taxes, including those from years before the sale, and that leaving the program makes the current year plus three earlier years payable with interest. A seller with such land should ask the Tax Assessor for its status before listing or accepting an offer.

  • Farm use needs 10 cultivated acres, and forest use needs 20 forested acres plus a management plan.
  • Farm income must average $1000 a year across the last three years.
  • A sale to an owner who cannot qualify can take the land out of the program.

How are vital record copies priced at this office?

Each certified copy of a birth, death or marriage certificate costs $10. The office takes online orders through Permitium/AIS, which adds a $3.35 convenience fee plus card fees, and it also accepts a mailed application.

The Vital Records page says birth and death files begin in October 1913 and marriage files in 1867.

How do property taxes connect to a deed in Edgecombe County?

The Tax Collector's office bills and collects real estate, personal property and vehicle tax for the county, 14 fire districts, one drainage district and eight towns. It also prepares statements of taxes due for attorneys and real estate professionals, which a closing attorney can request before a sale closes.

Questions about taxes paid or owed go to (252) 641-7810, and questions about a value go to the Tax Assessor at (252) 641-7855. Our Edgecombe County property tax guide covers rates, listing and appeals.

Which county office records a deed for a Rocky Mount or Tarboro home?

Recording follows the county where the land lies. A Tarboro house, the county seat, goes to the Edgecombe County office, and so does the Edgecombe side of Rocky Mount. The county's own description notes that Rocky Mount is divided between Nash and Edgecombe counties and is the largest municipality here, so check which side of the line your parcel sits on before you send the deed.

The excise tax statute adds a rule for a single parcel that crosses a county line: the tax is paid to the register in the county holding the greater share of the value. Edgecombe's tax rate table lists ten municipalities, including Princeville, Pinetops, Whitakers, Speed, Leggett, Conetoe, Macclesfield and Sharpsburg, so a parcel in a small town still needs its county confirmed.

Ask your closing attorney to confirm the parcel number and the county before the signing appointment, since the fee schedule's same day processing only helps when the paper reaches the right office.

What housing facts does the Census report for Edgecombe County?

Edgecombe County is small and rural. QuickFacts gives the following snapshot.

  • 49,121 residents in the July 2025 estimate, living in 23,604 housing units.
  • 60.8% of homes occupied by their owners, with a median value of $125,100.
  • Median household income of $51,265 and median rent of $858.
  • Adults 65 or older make up 23.1% of residents.
  • 53 building permits issued in 2025.

Recording fees are fixed by statute, so a $125,100 house pays the same page charge as a far costlier one. The excise tax is the line that follows the price.

More questions about Edgecombe County, NC Register of Deeds

Is there a fee to record a mortgage release in Edgecombe County?

No. The fee schedule lists a satisfaction at no fee, so releasing a mortgage at closing adds no recording charge.

What is the Edgecombe County excise tax rate?

The county prints $1.00 per $500.00. State law makes the seller pay it to the register of deeds before recording, and the office collects it along with the deed.

Does Edgecombe County record a deed that lacks a tax certification?

Only if the deed carries the attorney preparer statement. Otherwise the county resolution requires the Tax Collector's certification, and the statement must say a licensed North Carolina attorney prepared the deed and the closing attorney will pay delinquent taxes from proceeds.

How do I get a certified birth or death certificate in Edgecombe County?

Order online through Permitium/AIS or mail the application for certified copy. Each copy costs $10, and the online route adds a $3.35 convenience fee plus card fees.

Does the Edgecombe County register accept electronic filing?

Yes. The county accepts e-recording through Simplifile and lists CSC eRecording Solutions as another route, so ask your closing attorney or title company to submit the deed.

Forsyth County by the numbers

What land documents end up in the Forsyth County registry?

The registry is the county's permanent file of land title papers: deeds, deeds of trust and mortgages, satisfactions, plats, leases, notices of foreclosure and a few other filings.

The county's recording page also names assumed business names, rights of way, covenant agreements, UCC filings, affidavits, powers of attorney, separation and prenuptial agreements and living wills. The Clerk of Court keeps wills, divorces and estates. An heir selling an inherited Forsyth County house therefore files estate papers with the clerk first, then brings the deed to this office once authority is in place.

The volume behind that registry is large. The Census Bureau counts 159,925 households in the county (2020 to 2024), 2,875 building permits issued in 2025 and a median gross rent of $1,098, and each new house or refinance adds paper to the file.

How does a deed get filed with the Forsyth County office?

Carry in the signed original, or route it through an approved electronic vendor, during office hours on a business day.

  • At the counter: the paper comes back to you once it is recorded.
  • By mail: the office wants the precise fee in a business check, cashier's check or money order, written to the Forsyth County Register of Deeds, and a return envelope that is stamped and self-addressed. Do not mail cash.
  • Electronic: the sender files a submitter agreement with an authorized e-recording provider and completes a memorandum of understanding. The county lists CSC, EDL, EPN, IGS and Simplifile as vendors, and files must arrive by 4:30 p.m.

A buyer is protected only once the deed is on the registry. Until then, G.S. 47-18 leaves the transfer exposed to lien creditors and later purchasers, and the registration time decides who ranks first. The office only records, and staff cannot draft papers or give legal advice.

What does the Forsyth County office charge to record?

The charge depends on the kind of instrument and its page count, and the table lists each one as the county prints it.

Real estate fees from the Forsyth County Register of Deeds fee page
Filing typeFee on the page
Routine document$26 through page 15, then $4 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 through page 35, then $4 per page
Plat$21 per sheet
Non-standard document$25
SatisfactionNo fee
Several instruments sent as one$10 for each, on top of recording
Certified copy$5 for page one, $2 for later pages
Plain copy$.25 a page

The sheet also adds $2.00 per party beyond 20, counting attachments and exhibits. G.S. 161-10 sets these amounts and calls them complete and exclusive. At the counter the office takes business checks, official bank checks, money orders and credit or debit cards; cards carry a 3 percent charge with a $1.00 floor and cannot be used by phone. Personal checks and e-checks are turned away.

Who owes the excise tax when a Forsyth County deed is filed?

The seller, called the transferor in the statute, hands over the excise tax before the deed is recorded.

The charge in G.S. 105-228.30 is one dollar per $500 block of price or value, and a partial block is rounded up. The county general fund keeps one half. The state half is sent each month to the Department of Revenue, and the county may retain 2 percent of it. Land lying in two counties is taxed where the larger value sits.

Annual property tax is a separate matter. The county tax FAQ bills it to the January 1 owner and suggests clearing it at closing, so a settlement statement can show both items.

What layout rules does a Forsyth County filing have to follow?

A paper that misses the standard is charged an extra $25 as a non-standard document under G.S. 161-10.

  • Letter or legal size paper, typed or printed in black on white, one side only.
  • Leave three inches blank at the top of page one, keep side margins at half an inch or more, and use type of 9 points or larger.
  • The name of the instrument placed directly beneath that blank space.
  • Ink signatures in the acknowledgment, or else a certified copy of the signed original.
  • A grantee's current mailing address on a deed, and the drafter's name on the front of a North Carolina deed of trust.

These layout rules come from G.S. 161-14. Compare a draft to the list before it travels to the courthouse, since correcting a margin costs less than the surcharge.

How do I clear an old mortgage from the Forsyth County record?

The lender or noteholder cancels it by recording a satisfaction, and the office charges nothing to record one.

The county explains that a deed of trust or mortgage is a security instrument that is canceled once the debt is paid, while a deed is title and is never canceled. Cancellation is the responsibility of the owner or noteholder in the county where the instrument was recorded. The county lists several forms that can do the job: a satisfaction of security instrument, a trustee's satisfaction, a notice of satisfaction, a certificate of satisfaction and an affidavit of satisfaction.

Do not assume the lender has acted. The office states that payoff papers and satisfactions are not mailed to the borrower automatically after the loan is paid in full. A borrower can call the register of deeds to check that the loan is marked satisfied before ordering a copy of the record.

Where do tax maps and deed lookups fit in Forsyth County?

The tax office's parcel maps show lot lines, but the deed is the legal description to rely on.

The county's tax FAQ warns that parcel dimensions on tax maps are calculated for tax purposes only, and the acreage on a tax record may not match the deeded or platted acreage. To find legal lot dimensions, open the Deeds tab on the parcel's property detail page or use the register of deeds lookup. That is the practical step before a sale where a fence, a split lot or an old boundary dispute is in play.

What other services and fees does the Forsyth County office list?

Besides land records, the office charges for notary work and vital records, and it waives fees for some military papers.

  • Notary public: $10, and notarial acts are $5 for each signature, except when performed with an act that already carries a fee.
  • Comparing a copy for certification: $5.
  • Recording a military discharge and getting a copy: no fee, and the Thank a Veteran photo ID is also free.
  • Certified birth or death certificate: $10; marriage license: $60.

Heirs who need a certified death certificate pay $10 for it according to the fee page. Call the office to confirm which of these documents can be issued the same day.

More questions about Forsyth County, NC Register of Deeds

How much does the Forsyth County office charge for filing a document?

Nothing is added for a satisfaction of a deed of trust, and the other charges follow the county's fee sheet, which G.S. 161-10 backs.

Will the Forsyth County office accept my personal check?

No. The fee page rules out personal checks, counter checks and e-checks. Business checks, official bank checks, money orders and credit or debit cards work.

What is the cutoff for an e-filed deed in Forsyth County?

E-filed items need to land by 4:30 p.m. on a business day. Counter and mail filings follow the regular weekday hours.

Who covers the excise tax on a Forsyth County sale?

The seller pays it to the register of deeds first. The rate is one dollar per $500 block of value, and a partial block is rounded up.

Can staff at the Forsyth County registry help draft my deed?

No. The office records papers only, and state law keeps staff from giving legal advice or showing how to draft an instrument, so see an attorney.

Where is the Franklin County Register of Deeds?

The Franklin County Register of Deeds is at 283-B S. Bickett Boulevard in Louisburg, NC 27549, after a move made while the county courthouse is under construction. The mailing address is P.O. Box 545, Louisburg, NC 27549, the phone is 919-496-3500 and the fax is 919-496-1457.

The county describes the office as the custodian of real estate documents for Franklin County that reach back to 1776. For a sale anywhere in Franklin County, this is the office that holds the deed you received, the deed of trust on it and any plat or power of attorney tied to the parcel. Credit card payments are available. Because the office relocated recently, check the county page before you drive over with a document, and mail or e-record when you can.

What records does the Franklin County office keep?

Land records and vital records share one counter, and the land side matters most to a seller. For a home sale the land records matter most.

  • Deeds and deeds of trust, the documents that move title and secure a loan.
  • Powers of attorney, assumed names, maps and other papers connected to real property.
  • Military discharge records.
  • Birth and death certificates back to 1913 for events in Franklin County, and marriage certificates back to 1869, with a bond book that carries marriage information from 1779.

The office can also print birth and death certificates from the state system for North Carolina events, and it takes online orders for certified or regular copies of vital records through a county vendor. A seller dealing with an inherited house often needs a death certificate and the old deed from the same visit.

Does Franklin County require tax certification before a deed is recorded?

Yes. A deed moving real property is turned away unless the Tax Collector first certifies that no delinquent ad valorem or other administered tax is a lien on it. The county has applied this rule since April 1, 2015.

The Collections Department stamps deeds free of charge on weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm, excluding county holidays. There are three ways to get it done.

  • Walk the deed in to Collections before recording.
  • Mail it to the Franklin County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549, Attention: Tax Certification.
  • Use eRecording, which forwards deeds to the tax office on its own.

Electronic recordings that need the stamp must reach the tax department by 4:30 pm, so a closing that wraps up late should send its package early.

For a seller with back taxes, this is where the problem surfaces. The deed waits until the balance is cleared or the closing agent pays it out of the proceeds.

Can I record a Franklin County deed electronically?

Yes. Title companies, banks, attorneys and private individuals can all submit electronically, and every document type is accepted except UCC filings.

The county names three authorized providers: CSC eRecording Solutions (866-652-0111), Simplifile (800-460-5657) and the ePN eRecording Partners Network (888-325-3365). Its stated benefits are quicker recording, lower postage and courier spending, fewer rejected documents and added security. Closing attorneys normally choose the provider, so a seller rarely sets this up personally. Ask which day your closing will be recorded.

What will a Franklin County closing pay at the Register of Deeds?

Two charges apply at the counter: a page-based recording fee and a tax tied to the sale price.

For the recording fee, the state tier is $26 for a general instrument through page 15, with $4 added for every page after that. A deed of trust is $64 through page 35. Recording the release of a paid-off loan is free. A certified copy starts at $5, and a document that does not meet the standard format costs $25 more.

The deed tax comes to a dollar for each $500 of price or value, and a leftover fraction counts as another $500. The party giving up the property pays it at the register of deeds window ahead of recording, and the proceeds are divided between the county and state revenue. Your settlement statement will carry the final number.

Who handles each step when I sell in Franklin County?

Four parties handle separate pieces of a sale, as the county's own pages describe them.

Franklin County offices and the part each plays in a sale
OfficeWhat it doesContact
Register of DeedsRecords the deed and deed of trust, keeps land records and collects the recording fees919-496-3500
Collections Department (Tax Collector)Collects property tax and certifies there is no delinquent tax before a deed is recorded919-496-2172
Tax AdministrationSets values and handles real estate value appealsCounty Tax Office, through the Value Appeals page
eRecording providerSends the signed documents to the Register of Deeds electronicallyCSC, Simplifile or ePN

Sources for the table are the county Register of Deeds, Collections, Value Appeals and Electronic Recording pages listed below.

How do Franklin County tax bills affect a seller?

Real estate tax in the county is due each September 1, and the 2026 bills turn delinquent on January 6, 2027. The county mails bills in late July to early August, and money received before September 1 can earn a discount.

When a house sells after the bill arrives, the county tells the former owner to hand the bill to the buyer unless the former owner will pay it. Agreements between buyers, sellers and attorneys are not the tax office's concern, and because tax is a lien on real estate, the buyer wants everything settled at closing. A mortgage company that escrows tax still causes the bill to be mailed to the owner, and the county suggests checking in the second week of September that the lender paid. A Solid Waste Availability Fee is also billed per electrical connection. The commissioners set it each year, and part-time use of the home does not exempt you.

What is the process to dispute a Franklin County assessed value?

An owner files the Board of Equalization and Review form between January 1 and the board's adjournment, which usually falls in May. A change-of-value notice opens a separate 30-day window.

Staff look at the file first. Anything they cannot settle goes to the board, which mails its decision. The current revaluation took effect January 1, 2024, so the county wants evidence tied to that date. Higher bills, fixed income and market drops after January 1, 2024 are not legal grounds. Comparable properties with lower values, comparable sales before that date, unrepaired fire or storm damage, a denied septic permit and documented cleanup costs are. The owner carries the burden of proof. If the worry is affordability, ask the tax office about relief programs.

Why does recording order matter on a Franklin County sale?

Registration time decides priority. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, option, lease longer than three years and similar interests do not bind lien creditors or paying buyers until they are registered in the county where the land sits.

That explains why closings are timed around recording cutoffs, and why an unrecorded deed from a former owner can stall a new sale. If an inherited Franklin County house still shows the deceased relative as owner, check the index before you list and ask your closing attorney what must be recorded first.

More questions about Franklin County, NC Register of Deeds

Is the Franklin County Register of Deeds in the courthouse?

No, not at present. The office now sits at 283-B S. Bickett Boulevard in Louisburg while the courthouse is under construction. Mail goes to P.O. Box 545, Louisburg, NC 27549, and the phone is 919-496-3500.

Do I need a tax certification stamp to record a deed in Franklin County?

Yes, for any deed that transfers real property. The Tax Collector must certify there is no delinquent tax lien, free of charge on weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm. eRecording sends the deed to the tax office for you.

What does Franklin County charge to record?

The statewide tier applies: $26 through page 15 for a general instrument and $64 through page 35 for a deed of trust, plus $4 per extra page. Confirm with the office before mailing a long document.

Can a title company record electronically in Franklin County?

Yes. The office accepts all document types electronically except UCC filings, through CSC, Simplifile or the ePN network. The company or closing attorney normally handles the submission.

Who pays the North Carolina deed excise tax?

The seller pays it when the deed is brought in for recording. The rate is one dollar per $500 of value. The settlement statement shows the amount.

The public search is the place to look for deeds, deeds of trust and other property records. Some older records are not online, and the county asks you to visit or call for help with those. Uncertified copies can be pulled online. For a certified copy you can use the county's Certified Copy Request Portal, call 704-862-7681, email rod@gastongov.com or go to the office. A seller who needs a prior deed to prove how the family took title will usually want a certified copy for the closing attorney.

What else does the Gaston County office do besides deeds?

The office records and indexes deeds, plats, maps, deeds of trust, mortgages and other personal property documents, and it also issues marriage licenses and keeps birth and death certificates. It runs a passport service as well, and most of the money from passport fees goes to the U.S. Department of State, with a portion kept for the county general fund.

Paper records are kept in vaults, and digital copies sit on secure servers in the courthouse. The fees the office takes in for recording are far larger than its operating budget, so they help fund the county and the state general funds. If the office ever has a vacancy, the Board of County Commissioners appoints someone to fill the unexpired term.

What do copies and counter payments cost at the Gaston office?

Per the office's FAQ, plain copies run $0.25 a page. Certified copies start at $5 for page one, and each added page is $2.

Accepted ways to pay Register of Deeds fees:

  • Cash.
  • Business check or money order, made out to Gaston County Register of Deeds.
  • Debit or credit card.

Staff will point you to the books and help with the computers, though state law bars them from doing title research, and they cannot run a lien check for you. A lost deed can be replaced with a copy bought in person or requested in writing at the P.O. Box. Changing names on a deed means drawing a new deed, and the office suggests an attorney, since it keeps no legal forms for deeds or powers of attorney.

How much does the Gaston office charge to file a closing package?

The county's FAQ sends you to the uniform fee schedule, which tracks G.S. 161-10.

  • A general instrument is $26 through page 15, and each page past 15 adds $4.
  • A mortgage or deed of trust is $64 through page 35, with the same $4 for each extra page.
  • Recording a satisfaction of a paid-off loan costs nothing.
  • A plat is $21 a sheet.
  • Each extra instrument inside one document adds $10.

Transfer tax is a separate line, set by G.S. 105-228.30 at a dollar per $500 of price (any remainder counts as another $500). The seller pays it when the deed is presented.

What are the key Gaston County Register of Deeds details at a glance?

The table collects the practical details the county prints on its FAQ and records pages.

Gaston County Register of Deeds practical details from the county's FAQ and records pages
ItemDetail
Office hours8:30 am to 5 pm
Real estate recording cutoff4:45 pm
Marriage applicationsAccepted until 4:30 pm
Physical addressCourthouse first floor, 325 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Way, Gastonia
Mailing addressP.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053
Certified copy$5 first page, $2 each added page
PaymentCash, business check, money order, debit, credit

Can Gaston County help protect me from deed and lien fraud?

Yes. The office partners with the county's land records software provider to offer a free notification service. You sign up with a name and an email address, and you are alerted when a recording is filed in your name.

The county is clear that no system can prevent fraud. The alerts are meant to help you spot a bad filing quickly, which matters if you own a vacant, inherited or rental house in Gaston County and might not see the mail. Anyone who prepares a document for recording is also barred from including Social Security, bank account, card or similar numbers unless the law requires it. If one does appear, you can ask in writing for it to be removed from the online image under G.S. 132-1.10(g). There is no fee for that request, though the underlying filing stays in the public record.

How do Gaston County property values and appeals tie to a sale?

Gaston reappraises every four years. The most recent value date was January 1, 2023, and 2027 is the next one, preceded by an informal review before the Board of Equalization and Review sits.

Owners may file from January 1 until that board adjourns, typically the last week of April, or until 30 days after a Notice of Value Change if that is later. The Tax Office is at 128 West Main Avenue in Gastonia, phone 704-866-3158. Property tax is billed separately from anything the Register of Deeds collects and stays with the property until paid, so buyers expect it settled at closing. Our Gaston County property tax guide covers rates, relief programs and payment options in detail.

Why does the order of recording matter for a Gaston County seller?

Whoever registers first generally wins priority. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance or lease over three years does not bind lien creditors or paying buyers until it is on record where the land lies.

So before a buyer's deed goes in, confirm that earlier deeds in the chain, any estate documents and the release of a paid-off loan are all indexed. Releases are free to record. Ask your closing attorney to search the index and send the satisfaction of your old mortgage ahead of the sale.

What should an heir of a Gaston County house record before selling?

Settle the estate paperwork first. A deed signed by someone who does not yet hold title will not clear. For a small estate without a will, the state allows a small estate affidavit under G.S. 28A-25-1, filed where the decedent lived.

That route covers up to $20,000 in personal property after liens, and the affidavit lists every tract of land owned. Whatever route fits your family, the paper that gives you authority to sell lands in the Gastonia index, so build in time before the closing date.

More questions about Gaston County, NC Register of Deeds

Where do I mail documents to the Gaston County Register of Deeds?

Mail them to Gaston County Register of Deeds, P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053. For overnight service the county suggests an express envelope with a prepaid return envelope enclosed.

What is the cutoff for recording a deed in Gaston County?

Real estate recordings are accepted until 4:45 pm. The office itself is open from 8:30 am to 5 pm, and marriage applications stop at 4:30 pm.

What do Gaston County copies cost?

Black and white copies are $0.25 a page. Certified copies are $5 for page one with $2 on each page after.

Is the Gaston County records search online?

Yes. The county moved to a new public search system on May 28, 2026, with the old system's records carried over. Some older records are not digitized, so call 704-862-7681 for help.

Who owes the deed tax on a Gaston County closing?

The seller owes it when the deed is handed in, at a dollar per $500 of price. The settlement statement shows the dollar figure.

How do I reach the Graham County Register of Deeds?

The Graham County Register of Deeds is at 12 North Main Street, Robbinsville, NC 28771, with a mailing address of PO Box 406, Robbinsville, NC 28771. The phone is (828) 479-7971 and the fax is (828) 479-6902.

Staff are at the counter weekdays from 8:00 until 4:30, shutting for the noon hour. You can look at records without booking a time. The county warns that the office may run flex hours or close on some days for unforeseen reasons. On those days recordings are accepted in the Tax Office, so a seller should call ahead before planning a closing around a counter visit. Recording fees can be paid only in cash or by check. The Tax Office and the assessor work from 196 Knight Street in Robbinsville, and the assessor's phone is (828) 479-7963, so one trip can cover both the deed and any tax questions that come up at closing.

What does the Graham County office record?

It records legal documents, deeds, plats and certified documents, and it also handles notary oaths, marriages, births and deaths. The county says its records are kept under the North Carolina General Statutes and are open to the public.

For a house sale the useful items are the vesting deed, any deed of trust and the plat for the lot. The county's appraisal manual divides Graham County into three townships, Cheoah, Stecoah and Yellow Creek, and carries municipal codes for Robbinsville, Fontana and Santeetlah. Before you list, ask whether a plat for your parcel is on file, since a missing or dated boundary description can slow a closing.

What are the Graham County recording fees?

The county posts its own fee sheet on the Register of Deeds page, citing G.S. 161, and the real estate lines mirror the statewide schedule.

Graham County fee sheet, real estate lines
ItemCharge listed
Ordinary land record instrument$26 up to page 15, then $4 a page

Plat$21 per sheet
Copy of an instrument$5 certified first page, $2 each added; $0.25 plain

The sheet on the county page is dated October 1, 2011, with the deed of trust tier amended October 1, 2016, so check the current figure with the office before you mail a check.

How does Graham County show the deed tax?

Graham's sheet prints the state excise tax as $2 per thousand, the same as the one dollar per $500 in G.S. 105-228.30.

The seller pays it at the office just before recording, and the receipts are divided between the county and the state. The settlement statement should show it as its own line. Ask your closing attorney how it will appear on your deed.

When does Graham County bill property tax?

Bills go out July 1, come due September 1 and can be paid through January 5 with no interest.

  • Interest of 2% begins January 6, then 0.75% a month until paid.
  • A second real estate notice goes out each February.
  • Delinquent taxes are published in the Graham Star every April, and advertising fees are added to each listed bill.
  • Enforced collection can start any time after January 5: wage garnishment, bank attachment, a state debt setoff against income tax returns and lottery winnings, levy on rents and foreclosure.

Call the collector to confirm the amount before you pay a delinquent bill, because it will differ from the printed figure. The tax office lists (828) 479-7962 for foreclosure questions.

How do I pay Graham County property tax?

Pay in person, by phone or online. The county takes cash, credit card, money order or check, made out to Graham County, and a locked drop box sits at the side entrance of the building.

Cards carry a processor charge of 2.5% with a $2.00 minimum, none of which the county sets or receives. Partial payments and prepayments are accepted when the parcel or account number is noted on the check. With an escrow account the bill still comes to the homeowner, so pass a copy to your mortgage company. A returned check costs $25.00 or 10 percent, whichever is more.

What else does the Graham County tax office value and bill?

Besides land and buildings, the Graham County tax office values these items and takes exclusion applications.

  • Motor vehicles, boats, jet skis and houseboats.
  • Elderly, present-use value, religious and educational exclusions.
  • January listings of personal property and business personal property, improvements, business listing extensions and value appeals.

Motor vehicle tax is a separate bill payable to the NCDMV office at 74 S. Main Street in Robbinsville, phone (828) 479-4896. A houseboat sticker costs $5.00 and requires a copy of the pump out permit when you pay. A seller who owns a boat or houseboat should sort out those bills too, since a buyer will not want to inherit them.

What relief programs and reappraisal affect a Graham County sale?

The assessor and collector both hand out the elderly, disabled and veteran exclusion forms, and they go back to the assessor's office by June 1.

The county has a 2027 Schedule of Values, with market values set as of January 1, 2027, plus a present-use value schedule for farm and forest land. Under G.S. 105-277.1, a homeowner aged 65 or over, or totally and permanently disabled, may exclude whichever is greater, $25,000 or half of appraised value. G.S. 105-277.1C gives a disabled veteran a $45,000 exclusion with no age or income test. Personal property is listed from January 1 to January 31. The assessor's number is (828) 479-7963.

What happens in Graham County if property tax goes unpaid?

The lien runs with the parcel from the listing date. The county can pursue it with a foreclosure suit in the county of the land, modeled on a mortgage foreclosure, under G.S. 105-374.

The owner of record, a spouse and other lienholders receive service. Bidders compete at a courthouse-door auction, and the commissioner may ask for up to 20 percent down. A raised bid or exception must come within 10 days of the sale report, and redeeming before confirmation means paying the taxes with penalties, interest and costs. A seller who is behind should call the collector early, since newspaper advertising fees land on each listed bill.

What should a seller do before recording a Graham County deed?

Settle the tax bill, confirm that every old loan has a recorded satisfaction and have your closing attorney review the chain of title.

G.S. 47-18 ties priority to registration time, so the document recorded first in the county where the land lies generally takes precedence over later ones. Satisfactions record free in Graham County. If the person who held the deed has died, finish the estate paperwork first, because the buyer's lender will want proof of authority to sign in the index before funding.

More questions about Graham County, NC Register of Deeds

Can I pay Graham County recording fees by card?

No. The Register of Deeds page says only cash or checks are accepted for recording fees. Property tax payments are handled by the tax office, which accepts cards with a processor fee.

What if the Graham County office is closed when I need to record?

Call (828) 479-7971 first. The county says that when the office runs flex hours or closes, recordings are accepted in the Tax Office. Only cash or checks pay the recording fees.

What are the recording charges in Graham County?

The county sheet shows $26 up to page 15 for a land record instrument and $64 up to page 35 for a deed of trust, with $4 for each page beyond those points. Satisfactions are free.

When are Graham County property taxes due?

Bills mail July 1 and are due September 1. You can pay through January 5 without interest, and 2% interest starts January 6.

Is the Graham County transfer tax the same as the statewide rate?

Yes. The sheet prints $2 per thousand, which equals $1 for each $500 of price. The seller pays it before the deed is recorded.

Granville County by the numbers

Where is the Oxford recording office, and how do I phone it?

Go to the courthouse at 101 Main Street, Oxford, NC 27565, or call 919-693-6314. Letters go to P.O. Box 427 in the same city.

The county's online ordering page gives office hours as weekdays, 8:30 AM to 5 PM, and says a request sent after 4 PM waits until the next business day. For a sale, phone first and ask what the staff will need for your type of instrument, since they may not draft or repair documents.

The register of deeds is a countywide elected position, and G.S. 161-1 sets the term at two years.

Which documents does the Oxford office file?

Real estate records are the core of its work: deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names, powers of attorney and similar instruments. The county says each is recorded, indexed and scanned, and that deed records stretch back to 1746.

  • Land records: deeds, deeds of trust, plats and cancellations.
  • Personal records: births, deaths, marriages and marriage licenses.
  • Other filings: military discharges and notary commissions, plus the oath for Granville County notaries.

Staff run a recording counter, not a legal clinic. The office tells filers that state law bars it from practicing law, so it will not supply legal forms, coach you through filling one in, or say what a recorded document means legally. A North Carolina attorney can answer those questions.

What does Granville charge for vital records ordered online?

A certified birth, marriage or death certificate is $10.00 each, and an uncertified copy is $1.00, with a non-refundable $4 service and card fee on every online order. Records on the system begin in 1913.
