A copy of a valid photo ID is required with every request. Anyone newly married should wait 10 days after the ceremony before ordering a certified marriage copy. Death certificates may also be picked up by a funeral director who shows license proof.

Which fees apply when a Granville County deed is filed?

Expect two charges on a sale: a recording fee set statewide and the seller's excise tax. G.S. 161-10 makes the fee identical in all counties.

  • General instruments: $26.00 through page 15, plus $4.00 for each page beyond that.
  • Mortgages and deeds of trust: $64.00 through page 35, plus $4.00 per page beyond that.
  • Cancellations of a deed of trust: nothing to record.

The tax is $1.00 per $500 of consideration or value, rounding any remainder up, and G.S. 105-228.30 puts it on the transferor, due before recording. The county keeps half. For a tract in several counties, the one with the most value collects it. Because the tax is figured from the stated consideration, make sure the deed reflects the real contract.

Why should a Granville County deed be recorded promptly?

An unrecorded deed does not bind later buyers or lien creditors. G.S. 47-18 gives priority to the instrument registered first, measured by time, in whichever county holds the land.

That rule covers leases over three years, options and rights of first refusal as well. Seller-financed deals fall under Chapter 47H, which tells the seller to record the contract or a Memorandum of a Contract for Deed inside five business days and gives the purchaser until midnight of the third business day to cancel.

Is there protection against property fraud in Granville County?

Yes. The register of deeds' office provides a free alert tool, PropertyCheck, through its software vendor. Owners can ask for an email or text whenever a document is recorded that matches a name, a street address or a parcel number.

  • Register on the vendor's website.
  • Create alerts for each version of your name and for your spouse.
  • Add the property address and parcel number.

The county describes the scheme it guards against: a forger moves title into another name and records the paperwork while the real owner stays unaware. An alert does not block a filing. It gives you the chance to call 919-693-6314 and consult a lawyer fast.

Who may collect a vital record in person at the Oxford office?

Anyone picking up a record must show valid state-issued photo ID, and the county limits who may collect it for someone else. Online requests are first come, first served, with no refunds, and all messages about an order arrive by email.

  • The person named on the record.
  • A spouse, brother or sister, parent or step-parent, grandparent, or child, step-child or grandchild.
  • A funeral director, for a death certificate only, with proof of license.
  • An authorized agent, attorney or legal representative, who may be asked for proof.

Inaccurate order details can stop a request from being processed. Requests are handled on business days during office hours, and the vendor's help address for the ordering tool is on the ordering page.

What should a Granville County seller check in the records before closing?

Look up your own parcel on the Register of Deeds' online records first. The county says documents are available online and that copies can be had on request, so a seller can pull the vesting deed and any old loan paperwork without a trip to the courthouse.

  • The deed that put the property in your name, matching spelling and legal description.
  • Any deed of trust that was paid off but never cancelled of record.
  • Plats or easements that affect the parcel.
  • Assumed-name filings, if a business ran from the house.

A cleanup before listing is usually faster than a cleanup under a closing deadline. Where a recorded instrument looks wrong, call the office at 919-693-6314 to find out how it can be corrected, and bring an attorney in for anything that needs legal drafting.

How does the Oxford recording counter connect to the county tax office?

They are separate offices with a shared subject. Recording moves title, while Granville County Tax Administration, at 919-693-4181, sets the value and bills the tax. Under G.S. 105-355 unpaid tax becomes a lien on the parcel as of the January 1 listing date, so the balance should be settled by the time a new deed is recorded.

The county offers a 1.5% discount on current taxes paid between July 1 and August 15, and the bill is due September 1. A seller who closes in that window can ask the tax office what a prompt payment would save. Oxford, Butner, Creedmoor, Stem and Stovall all sit in this one county, so a deed for land in any of them is recorded at the single courthouse counter in Oxford.

How many homes and households does Granville County have?

QuickFacts lists 25,685 housing units in 2025 and 22,474 households across 2020 to 2024, averaging 2.52 residents each.

  • Veterans: 3,363.
  • Building permits in 2025: 257.
  • People living at the same address as a year earlier: 90.4%.
  • Midpoint monthly cost for owners paying a mortgage: $1,546.
  • Poverty rate: 13.5%.

These county figures give background on the market. Recording charges come from state law, so they stay the same whatever the numbers show.

More questions about Granville County, NC Register of Deeds

What will a standard deed cost to file?

The base is $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each page after, as G.S. 161-10 sets it. The seller adds the excise tax, which is $1.00 per $500 of value.

When can I come in?

The ordering page lists 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday to Friday. Call 919-693-6314 ahead of a visit for a deed that has unusual features.

Can staff prepare my deed for me?

No. The office is a recording office, and North Carolina law keeps its staff from practicing law, so it cannot supply forms or advise on legal effect. Hire an attorney for drafting.

Is a loan payoff cancellation free to record?

Yes. The state fee schedule lists no charge for a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage.

How far back do Granville deeds go?

The county page says deeds are available back to 1746, while vital records ordered online start in 1913.

Where do I file a deed for Greene County land?

File it at the Greene County Courthouse, 301 N. Greene Street, Snow Hill, NC 28580. The counter is staffed from 8:00 AM until 5:00 PM on weekdays, holidays excepted, and the phone is 252-747-3620. Letters go to PO Box 86.

The register of deeds describes the office as custodian of the county's real estate papers and vital records. On the land side it handles deeds, deeds of trust, maps, easements, leases, assignments and UCC fixture filings tied to real property. Notary commissions are logged there, and the office swears in notaries who reside in the county.

The county's rate page names three towns, Hookerton, Snow Hill and Walstonburg, and land in any of them is recorded at this single office.

Why does Greene County want a tax form before it records a deed?

The county ties recording to its tax records. Every deed submitted must carry a form signed off by the Greene County Tax Office, which the register of deeds' page calls the Deed Information form.

  • Who is giving and who is receiving the property, with addresses.
  • The street address and legal description, and buildings if the deed splits a parcel.
  • Any personal property that moves with the land, such as a mobile home.
  • Whether deferred tax value is involved, and how the two parties are related if so.
  • Unpaid prior-year tax and the current-year figure, filled in by the tax office.

The tax office also marks the document as a transfer, a split or a merge and assigns the parcel number. Instructions on the reverse of the form cover deeds where delinquent taxes exist, so phone the tax office at 252-747-3615 before heading to the courthouse if you owe back tax on the parcel.

Can a Greene County deed be e-recorded?

Yes, for nearly every deed. The office accepts electronic recording for all instruments except maps and highway rights-of-way, so a closing attorney can file from a distance.

The one difference involves the tax form. For electronic filings, the county says its tax office only approves Deed Information sheets inside the e-recording platform and asks filers not to deliver anything to the tax office by hand or mail. Paper filers get the signature first, then bring the packet to Snow Hill.

Index searches run from 1875 to the present on a site run by Courthouse Computer Systems. The register of deeds moved to that system in December 2025, and staff take questions at 252-747-3620.

What will the state fee schedule cost on a Greene County filing?

The charges come from G.S. 161-10 and are uniform statewide. A general instrument is $26.00 for its first 15 pages, a deed of trust is $64.00 for its first 35, and each extra page after those thresholds adds $4.00.

Recording a satisfaction of a deed of trust costs nothing, and plats run $21.00 a sheet. Items outside land records are priced separately by the county: a certified birth, death or marriage copy is $10.00 in cash, and a marriage license is $60, cash only.

Who owes the excise tax when a Greene County house is sold?

The seller does. The state levies $1.00 for each $500 of consideration or value, with a partial $500 counted whole (G.S. 105-228.30), and the transferor settles it with the register of deeds before the deed is filed.

The money is split between the county general fund and the state. Since the tax tracks the amount stated in the deed, check that figure against the sale contract. A deed bounced for a missing tax form or a wrong amount is not effective against later buyers and lien creditors until it is properly registered, according to G.S. 47-18.

What do Greene County tax rates and fees look like?

The tax department's 2026 page lists a county rate of $0.7835 per $100, with town and fire district charges stacked on top. The tax office is at 229 Kingold Boulevard, Suite B, Snow Hill (PO Box 482), phone 252-747-3615, open 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays.

Greene County 2026 rates and fees as the county prints them (https://greenecountync.gov/departments/tax/tax-rates/)

Eleven fire districts are listed, from Arba at $0.0700 to Fort Run at $0.1220, and a Middle Swamp service district shows $0.0910. Owners who hold mobile homes, boats, aircraft or unlicensed vehicles on January 1 must list them during January, and a late listing draws a ten percent penalty.

What else does the Greene County Register of Deeds handle besides deeds?

Vital records and licenses take up much of the counter. A certified birth, death or marriage copy costs $10.00 in cash when requested in person with a photo ID issued by the DMV.

  • By mail: send the signed application, a copy of your state photo ID, a $10.00 money order payable to the Greene County Register of Deeds (personal checks are refused) and a stamped return envelope to PO Box 86, Snow Hill, NC 28580.
  • Marriage license: each applicant 18 or older needs a certified birth certificate, a state photo ID or a passport for non-residents, a Social Security card, and a divorce decree or a spouse's death certificate if previously married. The fee is $60, cash only, and licenses are issued between 9:00 AM and 4:00 PM.
  • Licenses go back to the county that issued them, wherever the wedding takes place.

The office also offers a Thank-A-Vet program, an assumed business name filing, and a link for protection from property and mortgage fraud on its main page.

What does deferred tax mean on the Greene County deed form?

Item six on the county form asks whether deferred value is involved and, if so, how the grantor is related to the grantee. Item seven lists deferred taxes due by year, and the form warns that deferred taxes have not been calculated unless that section is filled in.

The tax office completes the lines for prior-year and current-year tax. If your parcel carries deferred value, ask the office to calculate the amount before the deed is signed, since the form treats uncalculated deferred taxes as unknown. Sellers should not leave that question for the closing table.

The form also asks for Social Security numbers but says disclosure is voluntary, based on federal law and N.C.G.S. 105-309 for tax administration.

How large and how affordable is Greene County?

QuickFacts shows 20,700 residents in 2025, a 1.2% gain on the 2020 estimates base, spread across about 267 square miles of land. That averages roughly 77 residents per square mile.

  • Owner-occupied share of homes: 66.5% (2020 to 2024).
  • Middle value of an owner's home: $117,400.
  • Middle gross rent: $853.
  • Middle household income: $53,244.
  • People in poverty: 19.9%.
  • Housing units in 2025: 8,070.

The middle home value here is about half that listed for Granville County and Greensboro on the same QuickFacts table. Building permits numbered 59 in 2025. Treat these as county averages, since one farmhouse or town lot can sit far from them.

More questions about Greene County, NC Register of Deeds

Which office records Greene County deeds?

The Register of Deeds in the Greene County Courthouse, 301 N. Greene Street, Snow Hill. It opens 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays except holidays and takes e-recordings for everything but maps and highway rights-of-way.

Does the Greene County tax office sign off on deeds?

Yes. The county's page states that every deed needs a tax form signed by the Tax Office. E-filers get that approval through the electronic platform.

How is the deed excise tax figured here?

At $1.00 per $500 of the consideration or value, with any remainder counted as a full $500. The seller pays the register of deeds before recording.

What number do I call for the register of deeds?

252-747-3620. The tax office has its own line, 252-747-3615, open 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays.

How old are the online Greene County indexes?

The county says online index searches cover 1875 through the present. The office began using a new records system in December 2025.

Guilford County by the numbers

Where can you reach Guilford County's recording office, and what are its hours?

There are two counters. Greensboro is at 201 W. Market St., with real estate and recording upstairs on the second floor. High Point is at 325 E. Russell Ave., Room 155. One number, 336-641-7556, serves both, and staff work weekdays from 8 until 5.

Mail can be addressed to P.O. Box 3427, Greensboro, NC 27402, or P.O. Box 1467, High Point, NC 27261. Rowan and Orange counties gave up land to form Guilford in 1771, and one set of land records now covers a Jamestown farmhouse, a Summerfield lot and a downtown Greensboro condo alike. General questions can go to guilforddeeds@guilfordcountync.gov, and the Census Bureau counted 562,234 residents in mid-2025.

What is the process for filing a deed with Guilford County?

Deliver a properly formatted deed with the recording fee and the excise tax, and the office puts it on record. Electronic submission works too, because Guilford accepts every real estate document sent through its approved e-recording vendors.

E-recording returns the book and page data plus a stamped image within minutes, and the system rejects a document immediately if it misses the state's recording standards. Paper filings must also show where to send the original after recording. The county's checklist for a standard document includes:

  • Letter or legal size paper, one-sided, black type on white stock.
  • Three blank inches above the text on page one, and a quarter inch of margin elsewhere.
  • Type no smaller than 9 point, with the instrument's title printed as a heading on the first sheet.
  • Pen entries for blanks and corrections are acceptable.

A document that fails any item draws the non-standard surcharge on top of the regular fee, so check the layout before you send it.

What fees does the Guilford County recording office collect?

Pricing starts at $26 for a general instrument of up to 15 pages, and a mortgage or deed of trust of up to 35 pages starts at $64. Each page beyond those limits adds $4. State law fixes those amounts, and the county's published table adds the smaller line items.

Guilford County Register of Deeds fee schedule, recording and copies
ItemFee printed by the county
Deed or other instrument$26 first 15 pages, $4 each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 first 35 pages, $4 each added page
Non-standard document$25 on top of the recording fee
Each added instrument in one document$10
Satisfaction of security instrumentNo fee
Plat or condominium map recording$21 per page
Certified copy$5 first page, $2 each added page

Source: the county's Recording and Real Estate page. An ordinary copy of a real estate record is 5 cents a page at the counter and $1 by mail. Under the statute these fees are the only ones allowed, and payment comes first.

The county's page lists a few extras that come up around a sale. A notary oath costs $10, and authenticating a notary costs $1 per notary per page. A map copy is 50 cents, and certified plats are $5 per copy. UCC filings run $38, or $45 above two pages plus $2 for each page past ten. The Guilford office takes only fixture-related UCC filings, and every other UCC filing goes to the Secretary of State in Raleigh.

Who pays the Guilford County deed excise tax?

The transferor does, handing it to the register before the deed goes on record. State law sets the rate at $1 per $500 of the price, counting any leftover fraction as a full $500, and the county's table shows deeds since August 1, 1991 at $2 per thousand, which is the same thing.

Half of the revenue stays in the county's general fund and the remainder is forwarded each month to the state revenue department. A closing statement lists the tax apart from the recording fee. The county's table also carries two older rate bands, $1 per thousand for 1968 through July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1968, which matter only when you read an old deed. For your own sale, get the exact figure from the closing attorney.

What happens to a payoff after it is recorded in Guilford County?

The loan stays visible against the title until someone records a satisfaction. North Carolina gives an unrecorded deed, option or long lease no priority over lien creditors or later buyers who paid value, and ranks competing claims by when they were registered.

Guilford describes three recordable forms of satisfaction, none of which costs anything to file:

  • A satisfaction signed by the secured creditor and acknowledged before a notary.
  • A trustee's or substitute trustee's satisfaction of the deed of trust.
  • An affidavit by a North Carolina attorney serving as satisfaction agent, for use when a lender never provides one.

The office stopped taking the original deed of trust and note as proof of payment. If an old lender's loan still shows open on your parcel, a recorded satisfaction clears it, and your attorney or the lender can arrange that.

How should Guilford County owners protect against forged deeds?

Enroll in the Property Fraud Alert. It emails notice when a document appears under a name variation you registered. The register must record a deed that meets the legal form once fees and taxes are paid, and the office does not test whether a signature is real.

The county names vacant or distressed homes, older owners and low-income owners as frequent targets. Its warning signs include a transfer you never signed, tax bills that stop arriving, and a default notice on a home with no mortgage. An owner who finds a bad deed should assemble the paperwork and report it to the Sheriff's Office or Greensboro or High Point police, the District Attorney, a real estate attorney and the register. The register cannot pull a recorded document from the index, so ask an attorney how to challenge it.

The county also advises checking credentials, reading contracts and considering a title search and title insurance.

Can the Guilford County register correct a mistake in a recorded deed?

Only indexing mistakes. G.S. 132-1.10 bars the office from changing a recorded instrument, so a misspelled name, a faulty legal description or a wrong loan amount in the document itself needs a corrective instrument prepared by your attorney.

The Indexing Correction Request form handles cases where the index differs from the document. Call 336-641-7556 or use the office email with questions. The corrective instrument is recorded at the usual fees. The recording page also carries a Personal Information Redaction section and a Real Estate Document Request form for copies.

How does Guilford County's housing stock look in the Census data?

QuickFacts counts 246,403 housing units for July 2025. For 2020 through 2024, the survey puts a middle-priced owned home at $259,900, the owner share of occupied homes at 59.9%, and median gross rent at $1,163.

The county's middle household earns $68,642 in 2024 dollars, and builders pulled 2,876 permits in 2025. For the tax side of a sale, read our Guilford County property tax guide.

More questions about Guilford County, NC Register of Deeds

Which phone number reaches Guilford's register of deeds?

336-641-7556, for the Greensboro office at 201 W. Market St. and the High Point office at 325 E. Russell Ave., Room 155. Staff are available on weekdays, 8 a.m. until 5 p.m.

What does a Guilford deed filing cost?

Expect $26 for an instrument of up to 15 pages and $4 for each page past that, plus a $25 surcharge when the document is non-standard. The seller also pays the excise tax before recording.

Is e-recording available through the Guilford register?

Yes. The office takes all electronically submitted real estate documents via approved vendors, sends back the recording details and a stamped image within minutes, and flags documents that miss the state standards.

Does the Guilford register verify a deed's authenticity?

No. A deed that meets the format rules is recorded once fees and taxes are paid. Owners can sign up for the free Property Fraud Alert and report forgeries to law enforcement and the District Attorney.

Do satisfactions of a mortgage carry a Guilford recording fee?

No. Satisfactions, affidavits of satisfaction and trustee's satisfactions are filed free of charge. The office does not accept the original deed of trust and note in their place.

Halifax County by the numbers

What services does Halifax County's recording office provide?

The office takes in, indexes and safeguards land records, and it also handles plats, UCC filings, vital records and assorted miscellaneous documents. The county says the elected register serves a 4-year term and leads a team of one assistant and four deputies.

Business runs from half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted. An online Register of Deeds Index Search is linked from the county site. Halifax County was carved from Edgecombe in 1758 along the Roanoke River, and the town of Halifax is the seat. The North Carolina Provincial Congress met in the town on April 12, 1776 and passed the Halifax Resolves, and the county still marks April 12 as Halifax Day. Census estimates count 46,534 people in the county for July 2025, and the county's 2026-27 budget ordinance appropriates $516,743 for the Register of Deeds.

How far back do Halifax County land records go?

Paper indexes reach to 1732, which is older than the county itself. Online, the index search offers three layers, as described on the county's Real Estate Records page:

  • Indexes and images of recorded real property documents from 1976 forward.
  • Historical real estate indexes for 1934 through 1975.
  • Survey maps dating from 1818.

Other record sets start at different points. Marriage records begin in 1825, and birth and death records begin in October 1913. Anything on a parcel that predates 1976 means working from the historical or hard-copy indexes.

Why does the Tax Collector sign off before a Halifax County deed is recorded?

Under a commissioners' rule that took effect January 1, 2016, the register will not accept a deed conveying real property unless the Tax Collector certifies that no delinquent ad valorem tax, or other tax the collector must collect, encumbers the parcel.

Staff need time to research each parcel, so the collector stops taking deeds at 4:30 in the afternoon. The collector's office is Tax Administration, 357 Ferrell Lane in Halifax, phone 252-583-2121. Do this step before you go to the register, since a deed without the certification is turned away. Our Halifax County property tax guide covers rates, appeals and relief.

What does Halifax County charge for recording documents?

The county's 2026-27 fee schedule lists $26 for an instrument up to 15 pages and $64 for a deed of trust or mortgage up to 35 pages, adding $4 for each page past those limits. State law fixes the same base amounts.

Halifax County Register of Deeds fees, fiscal year 2026-27 schedule
ItemFee as listed
Instrument, first 15 pages$26, then $4 per added page
Deed of trust or mortgage, first 35 pages$64, then $4 per added page
Non-standard form$25
Each added instrument in one document$10
SatisfactionNo charge
Plat recording$21 each
Certifying a recorded instrument$5 first page, $2 each added page
UCC filing, 1 to 2 pages / 3 to 10 pages$38 / $45

Source: Halifax County Schedule of Fees, fiscal year 2026-27. The schedule also lists $10 for each added index reference on an assignment, $2 per party past 20 distinct parties, and 25 cents a page for photocopies and scanned images. The statute treats its fee list as complete and exclusive, collected at filing.

What is the Halifax County deed stamp tax and who pays it?

On its fee schedule Halifax lists the excise stamp tax at $1.00 per $500 of consideration, with any remainder counted as another $500. State law matches that figure and places the duty on the party giving up title, who must pay before the deed is recorded.

Revenue is split in two. The county general fund keeps one portion, and the state revenue department receives the rest monthly after refunds and an allowance. The 2026-27 county budget ordinance shows $353,500 for the Register of Deeds among other taxes and licenses. A parcel split across county lines pays in the county holding the larger share. Ask your closing attorney for the exact amount before settlement.

Which recording rules affect Halifax County contracts for deed?

Registration is what gives a deed, option or long lease its force against lien creditors and later paying purchasers, and the order of registration sets priority among competing claims.

Seller financing falls under Chapter 47H when the buyer will make at least five payments besides the down payment, the seller keeps title, and the property is a principal dwelling of one to four families or a manufactured home with a price of $5,000 or more. Three features stand out:

  • The agreement must be written, signed and acknowledged.
  • The seller records it, or a Memorandum of a Contract for Deed, within five business days.
  • The buyer may cancel through midnight of the third business day, and a default notice must allow a cure date at least 30 days out.

Ask an attorney to draft any land contract and to confirm that it was recorded.

What else does the Halifax County register's office issue?

Beyond deeds, the county's 2026-27 fee schedule prices the vital records and notary services that run through the same counter:

  • Marriage license: $60, which includes the $35 state fee.
  • Certified copy of a birth certificate or a death certificate: $10 each.
  • Notary public oath administered: $10, and $5 to verify a commission.
  • Military service record: no charge.

The same schedule prices a certified plat copy at $5 for the first page and lists right-of-way plans at $21 for the first page and $5 for each added page.

How do Halifax County tax foreclosure sales connect to the land records?

A tax foreclosure auction ends with a deed, which the register records. The county publishes each sale notice on its Tax Foreclosures page, and bidding happens in the courthouse lobby at Halifax. A bid stays open to a higher one for 10 days, and the property goes as is.

The county cautions that purchasers take subject to taxes, assessments and liens held by parties who were not named defendants, and it suggests a title examination before bidding. If your own house faces a tax sale, selling before the auction keeps the price in your hands, and the register will record your deed once the tax certification is on file.

What housing figures does the Census report for Halifax County?

The Census Bureau's table counts 25,078 homes and apartments in July 2025 and 20,383 households between 2020 and 2024. Of occupied homes, 62.9% are owned. A middle-priced owned home carries a value of $106,200, and rent sits at a median of $813.

The middle household earns $45,590 in 2024 dollars, and seniors make up 25.2% of the population. Only 75 permits for new building were issued in 2025, a light year for construction in a county of 723.74 square miles of land.

More questions about Halifax County, NC Register of Deeds

When can I visit the Halifax County Register of Deeds?

Weekdays from half past eight to five, with holidays closed. The tax certification a deed needs is handled at the Tax Collector's office, which closes its deed window a half hour before the register's counter.

How much will a Halifax County filing run?

The 2026-27 county schedule shows $26 for up to 15 pages plus $4 for every added page, and $25 more for a non-standard form. The seller also owes the excise stamp tax of $1.00 per $500 of value.

What can make the Halifax County register reject a deed?

A missing certification from the Tax Collector is one reason. A county rule effective January 1, 2016 bars the register from accepting a deed until delinquent taxes are cleared and certified, so visit Tax Administration first.

How old are the land records the Halifax County register holds?

Paper indexes go back to 1732. Online search covers recorded documents from 1976 forward, historical indexes for 1934 through 1975, and survey maps from 1818.

Is recording a satisfaction of a mortgage free in Halifax County?

Yes. The county's fee schedule shows no charge for satisfactions, consistent with state law. A deed of trust itself starts at $64 for its first 35 pages.

What does the Yadkin County Register of Deeds handle?

This office in Yadkinville keeps the county's land records: deeds, deeds of trust, maps and related filings. State law opens those records to public inspection. The staff also copy and certify birth, death and marriage certificates, issue marriage licenses and swear in notaries.

A sale is only fully protected once the deed is on the books. Under G.S. 47-18, an unregistered conveyance loses to lien creditors and later buyers who paid value, and whoever registers first generally ranks first.

The county web page urges electronic recording for every document. Marriage licenses and notary oaths run by appointment through 336-849-7904. The register of deeds is an elected post, and the excise tax on deeds is collected at this same counter.

How does a deed get on record after a Yadkin County sale?

Usually the attorney or title company at the closing table sends it electronically. The register accepts every document type except maps by e-recording. Any firm wanting to submit must go through Simplifile, CSC or ePN and complete a submitter agreement that the provider passes to the county.

The Yadkin County tax office page has a one-line instruction for deed work: consult your attorney, then it links to the Register of Deeds. Sellers in Yadkinville, Jonesville, East Bend or on a rural road in between therefore rarely deal with the recording desk themselves.

  • Ask whether your closing firm already has an e-recording agreement with Yadkin County.
  • Find out who is writing the check for the excise tax, since the statute assigns it to the seller.
  • Keep the recording confirmation as proof of the date and time of registration.
  • Bringing paper instead? Phone the office before you drive, because no walk-in recording hours appear on the county page.

What does recording cost at the Yadkin County Register of Deeds?

A single statewide schedule applies here. G.S. 161-10 prints one schedule for the whole state, calls it complete and exclusive, and requires payment up front.

Register of Deeds charges in G.S. 161-10 that touch a house sale
DocumentAmount printed
Deed, pages 1 through 15$26.00
Mortgage, pages 1 through 35$64.00

Count the pages in your deed and exhibits before closing, because the $4.00 charge starts on the sixteenth page of a general instrument.

Who owes the excise stamp on a Yadkin County deed?

The person transferring the house. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the rate at one dollar per five hundred dollars of value. Payment is due at the register's counter ahead of the filing.

Collections are divided evenly. Half stays with the county. The state's half is remitted monthly, and the county may retain 2 percent of it. The closing statement lists the dollar figure that applies to your price.

If a house passes as a gift or between relatives, ask the office how a stated value is treated before anyone signs.

Where does the tax office fit in with the Register of Deeds?

They are separate counters. The Yadkin County Tax Department in Yadkinville lists and bills property, takes exemption applications and keeps the parcel maps. The register of deeds only records the paper. The tax office page announces a 2027 revaluation and points deed questions back to an attorney and the Register of Deeds.

For billing and payment questions, the tax office takes calls at 336-849-7903. It lists an August discount of 2 percent, plus a solid waste fee of $76.00 per household, or $38.00 with the elderly exemption. Statewide, taxes fall due September 1, and interest starts January 6 (G.S. 105-360).

Which other documents are recorded at the Yadkin County Register of Deeds?

More than deeds. Under G.S. 47-18, options, leases beyond three years and rights of first refusal must be registered before they bind a later buyer. A seller who gave a buyer an option months ago should check that it was recorded, since an unrecorded one may not hold up against a new purchaser.

A seller-financed sale is the other case worth knowing. North Carolina's Chapter 47H covers a contract for deed with five or more payments, where the seller keeps title. Written and acknowledged terms are required, the buyer gets a three-business-day cancellation window, and the seller records the contract or a memorandum within five business days. A forfeiture notice has to allow at least 30 days to cure (Chapter 47H).

  • Satisfactions of a deed of trust record for no fee under G.S. 161-10, so paying off a mortgage costs nothing at this office.
  • For a parcel split between counties, the excise tax goes to the county holding the greater value.
  • An estate sale may require a small estate affidavit to list each tract the decedent owned.

What does the Yadkin County housing picture look like?

The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate for Yadkin County is 38,325 people, a 3.0 percent gain over 2020 that has not quite regained the 38,406 of 2010. About 111 people live on each of its 334.94 land square miles, and there are 17,697 housing units.

Owners live in 76.9 percent of Yadkin County homes. Survey data for 2020 to 2024 show a median home value of $181,200, owner costs of $1,177 monthly with a mortgage, and rent of $766. Households earn a median $62,932, and 14.5 percent of people fall below the poverty line. Adults 65 and over are 22.4 percent of residents and 1,966 are veterans, so the age-based and veteran programs reach many owners.

Employers numbered 650 in 2023 with 8,235 jobs among them, and the average commute is 29.6 minutes. New construction is slow, with 116 building permits in 2025. Many sales involve inherited or older houses; for an estate, the clerk of superior court can say who has authority to sign.

How do Yadkin County's economy and demographics shape a home sale?

Retail sales were $338,224 thousand in 2022, or $9,018 per resident, according to the Census Bureau, a lower per-person figure than a county with a large shopping district would show. Health care and social assistance brought in receipts of $66,701 thousand and transportation and warehousing $57,494 thousand. The county had 2,727 nonemployer businesses in 2024, which fits a place with many self-employed households.

Of adults 25 and older, 86.6 percent hold a high school diploma and 17.5 percent a bachelor's degree. Home internet is common, with 87.9 percent of households subscribed to broadband, a point for buyers planning to work from home.

For a seller, the practical point is a buyer pool drawn from nearby employers and commuters. Owners facing a tax lien can look at the county's Tax Foreclosure Sales page to see how auctions are listed, and redemption remains possible before a sale is confirmed.

More questions about Yadkin County, NC Register of Deeds

Does Yadkin County charge a transfer tax on a sale?

Yes. The seller owes a deed excise tax, paid to the register at filing. The rate is one dollar for each five hundred dollars of value.

Can a Yadkin County deed be recorded electronically?

Yes, any document except a map. The attorney or title company must first sign a submitter agreement through Simplifile, CSC or ePN. For paper filings, phone 336-849-7904.

Does it cost anything to record a satisfaction of a mortgage in Yadkin County?

No. G.S. 161-10 sets no charge for a satisfaction, so the payoff paperwork is free to file.

How long does a buyer under a Yadkin County contract for deed have to cancel?

Through midnight of the third business day. After that, the seller has a five-business-day window to record.

Is a Yadkin County revaluation coming?

Yes, the county tax page says a 2027 revaluation is underway. Counties must reappraise all real estate on an eight-year cycle at the longest.
